definition: To leave behind or give up completely, often under stressful or difficult circumstances; to desert someone or something you are responsible for.

mnemonic.story_en: A BAND ON the road just walked away and left all their heavy equipment behind — they decided to abandon the tour because it was too exhausting.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一個樂團（A BAND）在巡演途中突然把所有樂器丟在路（ON the road）上走人，決定徹底「放棄」這場令人疲憊的演出。

example: Due to the rising water levels, the driver had no choice but to abandon her car in the middle of the flood.

definition: To formally and officially put an end to a system, practice, or institution, typically through legal or political means.
definition_zh: 廢除（制度、法律等）；宣告無效

mnemonic.story_en: A BULL ISH law was so stubbornly unfair and powerful like an angry bull that the citizens organized a massive protest to abolish it.
mnemonic.story_zh: 那條法律像公牛（BULL）一樣蠻橫（ISH），人民忍無可忍，決定起義將這項惡法「廢除」。

example: Slavery was finally abolished in the United States after years of intense political struggle and a bloody civil war.

definition: Existing in thought or as an idea but not having a physical or concrete existence; difficult to understand because of its complexity.
definition_zh: 抽象的；非具體的；深奧的

mnemonic.story_en: ABS TRACT — imagine trying to pull (tract) your physical abs away from your body to place them on a table. You can't do it physically — it's an abstract idea!
mnemonic.story_zh: 想像你想把腹肌（ABS）從身體裡拉（TRACT）出來單獨觀察，這在現實中是不可能的——因為這只是一個「抽象」的概念。

example: The concept of beauty is purely abstract and varies significantly from one culture to another.

definition: To increase in speed or cause something to happen more quickly than originally expected.

mnemonic.story_en: AC + CELERY + ATE — a competitive race car driver ate a magical piece of celery and his vehicle suddenly accelerated to lightning speed.
mnemonic.story_zh: 賽車手在吃了（ATE）特製芹菜（CELERY）後，車子瞬間開始「加速」，化作一道閃電。

example: Technological advancements in AI are expected to accelerate economic growth across the globe over the next decade.

definition: To provide lodging or sufficient space for someone; to fit in with or adjust to the particular needs or wishes of others.
definition_zh: 容納；提供住宿；配合需求；使適應

mnemonic.story_en: A COMMA DATE — when planning a group date, you must put commas between everyone's busy schedules to accommodate their different needs.
mnemonic.story_zh: 安排多人聚會（DATE）時，必須在不同人的時間表裡加逗號（COMMA）留空檔，才能「配合」並「容納」大家的各種需求。

example: The grand ballroom is large enough to accommodate more than 500 guests for the wedding ceremony.

definition: to gather or build up gradually over time

mnemonic.story_en: A KUMQUAT LATE — kumquats kept piling up because they arrived late and accumulated in the corner.
mnemonic.story_zh: 金桔（KUMQUAT）一直遲到（LATE），堆在角落越來越多，就這樣積累成一座小山。

example: Dust accumulates quickly if you don't clean regularly.

definition: correct in all details; exact

mnemonic.story_en: ACU + RATE — an acupuncturist rates each needle placement carefully to be accurate.
mnemonic.story_zh: 針灸師（ACU）仔細評估（RATE）每一針的位置，務求精確。

example: The weather forecast was accurate this time.

definition: to successfully reach a desired goal or result

mnemonic.story_en: A CHIEF who climbs to the top has achieved their goal — reaching the head position.
mnemonic.story_zh: 酋長（CHIEF）爬上頂峰，達成目標——登上首位，成就非凡。

example: She achieved her dream of becoming a doctor.

definition: to accept or admit the existence or truth of something

mnemonic.story_en: AC + KNOWLEDGE — to face toward knowledge and admit you know something. That's acknowledging it.
mnemonic.story_zh: 面向知識（KNOWLEDGE）並承認你知道——這就是「認可、承認」的動作。

example: He acknowledged his mistake in front of the team.

definition: to become adjusted to new conditions; to modify

mnemonic.story_en: A DAP T-shirt — you adapt your outfit to fit any situation, always apt for the moment.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一件百搭（DAP）的T恤，無論什麼場合都能適應——這就是ADAPT。

example: Animals must adapt to survive in changing environments.

definition: satisfactory or acceptable in quality or quantity

mnemonic.story_en: ADD E QUIT — add just enough to not quit. That's adequate — enough to keep going.
mnemonic.story_zh: 加（ADD）剛好夠讓你不放棄（QUIT）的量——這就是「adequate」，剛剛好。

example: Make sure you get adequate sleep before the exam.

definition: next to or adjoining something else

mnemonic.story_en: A JAY SENT next door — a blue jay was sent to live in the adjacent nest.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一隻藍鵲（JAY）被派（SENT）到隔壁的巢——住在相鄰的地方。

example: The library is adjacent to the main building.

definition: to publicly support or recommend; a person who supports a cause

mnemonic.story_en: ADD A VOICE + ATE — an advocate adds their voice to the table and eats with those they fight for.
mnemonic.story_zh: 倡導者（ADVOCATE）為弱勢加上一把聲音（VOICE），和他們同桌而食。

example: She advocates for equal rights in education.

definition: open to more than one interpretation; unclear

mnemonic.story_en: AMBI + GU + OUS — ambidextrous people can go either way, just like ambiguous sentences.
mnemonic.story_zh: 雙手靈巧（AMBI）的人兩邊都能用，模糊的（AMBIGUOUS）句子也是兩邊都說得通。

example: His answer was ambiguous — we couldn't tell if he agreed.

definition: having a strong desire for success or achievement

mnemonic.story_en: AM BITCH US — an ambitious person aggressively goes after every goal, running in all directions.
mnemonic.story_zh: 有抱負的人四處奔走（AMBI-去四方）爭取目標，鬥志高昂。

example: She is ambitious and plans to become CEO by 30.

definition: to examine something in detail to understand it

mnemonic.story_en: ANA + LYZE — Ana loosens every knot to analyze what's inside each one.
mnemonic.story_zh: 安娜（ANA）把每個結都解開（LYZE），仔細分析裡面裝著什麼。

example: Scientists analyze data to find patterns.

definition: to expect or predict something before it happens

mnemonic.story_en: ANTI + CAPE — a superhero prepares their anti-cape before the villain arrives, anticipating the attack.
mnemonic.story_zh: 超級英雄事先準備好反斗篷（ANTI-CAPE），提前預見（ANTICIPATE）了反派的到來。

example: We anticipate high demand for the new product.

definition: clearly visible or understood; obvious

mnemonic.story_en: A PARENT — it's apparent who the parent is at the school play. They're obviously cheering the loudest.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一眼就能認出誰是家長（A PARENT）——他們在學校表演時叫得最大聲，顯而易見。

example: It was apparent that she hadn't slept.

definition: to recognize the value or quality of something; to be grateful

mnemonic.story_en: A PRICE + EAT — you appreciate a meal so much you'd pay any price just to eat it again.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你太感激這頓飯（EAT）了，願意付任何價格（PRICE）再吃一次——這就是「appreciate」。

example: I really appreciate your help with this project.

definition: suitable or proper in the circumstances

mnemonic.story_en: A PROPER + EIGHT — an appropriate score is a proper 8 out of 10. Not too high, not too low.
mnemonic.story_zh: 最適當（APPROPRIATE）的分數就是剛好得八（EIGHT）分——不高不低，恰到好處。

example: Please wear appropriate clothing to the interview.

definition: based on random choice rather than reason or logic

mnemonic.story_en: AR + BIT + RARY — an arbitrator flips a bit (0 or 1) randomly, making arbitrary decisions with no logic.
mnemonic.story_zh: 仲裁者（ARBITER）隨便丟一枚硬幣來決定結果——完全武斷、毫無邏輯。

example: The rules seemed arbitrary and unfair.

definition: a particular part or feature of something

mnemonic.story_en: ASS + PECK T — a bird pecks at every aspect of a painting, looking at each part carefully.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一隻鳥啄（PECK）著畫的每個部分仔細觀看——每一個面向（ASPECT）都不放過。

example: Consider every aspect of the problem before deciding.

definition: to evaluate or estimate the nature or quality of something

mnemonic.story_en: A + SESS — a professor sits beside you in a session to assess your performance.
mnemonic.story_zh: 教授坐在你身旁（坐下-SED）一起上課（SESSION），評估你的表現。

example: Teachers assess students through exams and projects.

definition: to suppose something to be true without proof

mnemonic.story_en: ASS + U + ME — when you ASSUME you make an ASS out of U and ME. Classic reminder.
mnemonic.story_zh: ASSUME 拆開是 ASS + U + ME——亂假設只會讓你（U）和我（ME）都出醜（ASS）。

example: Don't assume you know what someone is thinking.

definition: a settled way of thinking or feeling about something

mnemonic.story_en: AT + IT + TUDE — your attitude is how you are 'at it' — the emotional state you bring to things.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你做事的「姿態」（AT IT）就是你的態度（ATTITUDE）——你帶著什麼狀態面對事物。

example: A positive attitude can change everything.

definition: to regard something as caused by; a quality or feature

mnemonic.story_en: A TRIBUTE — you attribute success to someone by paying them a tribute for their qualities.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你以致敬（TRIBUTE）的方式，將成功歸功於某人，讚揚他的特質（ATTRIBUTE）。

example: She attributed her success to hard work and luck.

definition: the power or right to give orders and make decisions

mnemonic.story_en: AUTHOR + ITY — an author has authority over their story. They created it, they control it.
mnemonic.story_zh: 作者（AUTHOR）對自己的故事擁有最高權威（AUTHORITY）——他創造它，他掌控它。

example: The police have the authority to make arrests.

definition: an advantage or profit; to receive advantage from

mnemonic.story_en: BENE + FIT — when something is beneficial, it's a good fit for you. It fits you well.
mnemonic.story_zh: 有益的事物就是很合你的（FIT），合身又合意——這就是「benefit」帶來的好處。

example: Exercise has many benefits for your health.

definition: an unfair preference or prejudice for or against something

mnemonic.story_en: BY + ASS — judging by someone's ass (appearance) instead of merit is pure bias.
mnemonic.story_zh: 只用外表評判一個人，完全是偏見（BIAS）——走斜路而非直路。

example: News coverage often shows political bias.

definition: the maximum amount something can contain; ability

mnemonic.story_en: CAP + CITY — a city with a cap on how many people it can hold. That cap is its capacity.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一座城市（CITY）戴上帽子（CAP）限制人口——帽子的大小就是它的容量（CAPACITY）。

example: The stadium has a capacity of 80,000 people.

definition: a difficult task or situation; to question or dispute

mnemonic.story_en: CHAL + LENGE — a challenger has long legs (LENGE sounds like long) and always runs toward the challenge.
mnemonic.story_zh: 挑戰者有長腿（LENGE→LONG），永遠朝挑戰（CHALLENGE）奔去，從不退縮。

example: Learning a new language is a big challenge.

definition: a fact or condition connected with an event or action

mnemonic.story_en: CIRCUS + STANCE — your stance in the circus ring is your circumstance — what's standing around you.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你在馬戲團（CIRCUS）裡的姿勢（STANCE）就是你的處境——周圍站著什麼就是你的「情況」。

example: Under the circumstances, we had no choice.

definition: to work jointly with others on a project

mnemonic.story_en: CO + LAB + ORATE — two scientists share a lab and orate their ideas together. They collaborate.
mnemonic.story_zh: 兩位科學家共用一間實驗室（LAB），一起高談闊論（ORATE）——這就是合作（COLLABORATE）。

example: The two companies collaborated on a new product.

definition: consisting of many interconnected parts; difficult to understand

mnemonic.story_en: COM + PLEX — a complex is like a complex of buildings woven together — many parts intertwined.
mnemonic.story_zh: 複合式建築群（COMPLEX）就是很多棟樓交織（PLEX）在一起——複雜而相互連結。

example: The math problem was too complex for me.

definition: an abstract idea or general notion

mnemonic.story_en: CON + CEPT — a concept is something you've grasped (CEPT from capere). You captured the idea.
mnemonic.story_zh: 概念（CONCEPT）就是你「抓住」（CEPT）的思想——把一個想法完整地握在手中。

example: The concept of democracy is taught in schools.

definition: to bring to an end; to arrive at a judgment

mnemonic.story_en: CON + CLUE + D — with all the clues (CON + CLUE) gathered, the detective finally concluded.
mnemonic.story_zh: 偵探蒐集所有線索（CLUE）之後，終於得出結論（CONCLUDE）——把案子的門關上。

example: The report concludes that pollution is rising.

definition: to establish the truth or correctness of something

mnemonic.story_en: CON + FIRM — a firm (company) is confirmed when all parties make it solid and official.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一家公司（FIRM）成立正式確認（CONFIRM）時，所有事項都變得穩固牢靠。

example: Please confirm your attendance by Friday.

definition: a serious disagreement or clash; to be incompatible

mnemonic.story_en: CON + FLICT — con artists and police flick at each other — constant conflict and clashing.
mnemonic.story_zh: 兩方人馬對打（FLICT=打擊），碰在一起（CON）就產生衝突（CONFLICT）。

example: There was a conflict between the two teams.

definition: a result or effect, typically a negative one

mnemonic.story_en: CON + SEQUENCE — a consequence is the sequence that follows your action. Every con has a sequence.
mnemonic.story_zh: 後果（CONSEQUENCE）就是跟在你行動後面的序列（SEQUENCE）——每個決定都帶著它的後續。

example: Cheating has serious consequences.

definition: acting or done in the same way over time; compatible
definition_zh: 一致的；前後連貫的；持續的

mnemonic.story_en: CON + SISTER + T — your consistent sister always stands firm in her habits, never changing.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你的姐妹（SISTER）總是一起（CON）穩穩站著（T），從不改變——她很有一致性（CONSISTENT）。

example: Be consistent in your practice to improve.

definition: to compare in order to show differences; a striking difference

mnemonic.story_en: CONTRA + ST — two countries (contra) stand facing each other to show their contrast.
mnemonic.story_zh: 兩個對立（CONTRA）的東西站（ST=STAND）在一起比較——這就是「對比」（CONTRAST）。

example: The contrast between the two paintings is striking.

definition: to give something in order to help achieve or provide something

mnemonic.story_en: CON + TRIBUTE — to contribute is to give a tribute alongside others toward a shared goal.
mnemonic.story_zh: 貢獻（CONTRIBUTE）就是和大家一起（CON）獻上（TRIBUTE）你的心力，共同完成目標。

example: Everyone must contribute to make the project succeed.

definition: prolonged public disagreement or heated debate

mnemonic.story_en: CONTRA + VERSE — controversy is like two verses of a song turning against each other in debate.
mnemonic.story_zh: 爭議（CONTROVERSY）就像兩段歌詞（VERSE）互相對立（CONTRA）翻轉——吵個不停。

example: The new law sparked major controversy.

definition: to cause someone to believe that something is true

mnemonic.story_en: CON + VINCE — Vince completely conquered your doubts. He convinced you with every argument.
mnemonic.story_zh: 文斯（VINCE）完全（CON）征服了你的疑惑——他說服（CONVINCE）了你每一個顧慮。

example: She convinced me to try the new restaurant.

definition: willing to work with others toward a shared goal

mnemonic.story_en: CO + OPERA + TIVE — a cooperative cast puts on an opera together, each playing their part.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一群合作的演員（CO）一起演出歌劇（OPERA）——每個人都扮好自己的角色，配合無間。

example: The students were cooperative during the group project.

definition: principles or standards used to judge or decide

mnemonic.story_en: CRY + TEAR + IA — the criteria were so strict, candidates cried tears during the selection.
mnemonic.story_zh: 評選標準（CRITERIA）嚴苛到讓應徵者哭出眼淚（CRY + TEAR）——門檻太高了。

example: What criteria will be used to select the winner?

definition: extremely important; decisive

mnemonic.story_en: CRUEL + AL — it may seem cruel, but that crucial decision at the crossroads defines everything.
mnemonic.story_zh: 站在十字路口（CRUX）的那個殘酷（CRUEL）時刻——那個至關重要（CRUCIAL）的決定左右一切。

example: Sleep is crucial for good health.

definition: a system of money in general use; being current/up-to-date

mnemonic.story_en: CURRENT + CY — currency is like a current of water that flows and keeps things running in an economy.
mnemonic.story_zh: 貨幣（CURRENCY）就像水流（CURRENT）——在經濟中持續流動（CURRERE），驅動一切運轉。

example: The dollar is the world's most traded currency.

definition: a formal discussion with opposing arguments; to argue about

mnemonic.story_en: DE + BAIT — in a debate, each side baits the other with arguments, trying to bring them down.
mnemonic.story_zh: 辯論（DEBATE）中，雙方互相用論點釣魚（BAIT）——想把對方的論述打倒（DE）。

example: The two candidates had a heated debate on TV.

definition: to decrease gradually; to politely refuse

mnemonic.story_en: DE + CLINE — a declining graph line bends down. Sales declined and the line went downhill.
mnemonic.story_zh: 下降的圖表線（CLINE）朝下（DE）彎去——銷售額下滑（DECLINE），曲線一路往下走。

example: She declined the job offer politely.

definition: to state the exact meaning of; to describe the nature of

mnemonic.story_en: DE + FINE — to define is to draw a fine (thin) line around a word, setting its limits completely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 定義（DEFINE）就是在一個詞的周圍畫出清晰的細線（FINE），完全（DE）劃定它的邊界。

example: Can you define the word 'ambiguous'?

definition: to clearly show or prove something; to take part in a protest

mnemonic.story_en: DEMON + STRATE — a demon on stage demonstrates its powers, showing everyone completely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一個惡魔（DEMON）站上舞台（STRATE）施展技能——完整展示（DEMONSTRATE），讓所有人看清楚。

example: The teacher demonstrated how to solve the equation.

definition: to obtain or develop something from a source

mnemonic.story_en: DE + RIVE — to derive is to pull something from the river (rivus), drawing it downstream from its source.
mnemonic.story_zh: 從河流（RIVE）的源頭往下引水（DE）——「derive」就是從源頭導出、取得某物。

example: Many English words are derived from Latin.

definition: to ascertain or establish exactly; to cause something to occur

mnemonic.story_en: DE + TERMINAL — at the terminal (final point), you determine your destination completely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在終點站（TERMINAL）做出最終（DE）決定——這就是「determine」，確立方向，劃定終點。

example: Scientists are trying to determine the cause of the disease.

definition: to grow or cause to grow gradually; to create over time

mnemonic.story_en: DE + VELOP + E — to develop is to unwrap (un-envelop) something hidden inside, letting it grow.
mnemonic.story_zh: 發展（DEVELOP）就是把包裹（VELOP=envelope）打開，讓裡面的潛能慢慢展開生長。

example: The company plans to develop a new app.

definition: recognizably different in nature; clear and unmistakable
definition_zh: 截然不同的；明顯的；獨特的

mnemonic.story_en: DIS + TINCT — distinct things are pricked apart with a distinct tint (color), clearly different.
mnemonic.story_zh: 截然不同（DISTINCT）的東西，被刺（TINCT）開（DIS）分成兩邊，顏色各異，清楚可辨。

example: The two paintings have distinct styles.

definition: a range of different people, ideas, or things

mnemonic.story_en: DIVERSE + CITY — a diverse city is full of people turning in different directions, all coexisting.
mnemonic.story_zh: 多元的城市（DIVERSE CITY）裡，每個人都朝著不同方向（VERTERE）走——這就是多樣性（DIVERSITY）。

example: The school values cultural diversity.

definition: most important, powerful, or influential
definition_zh: 佔主導的；支配的；顯性的

mnemonic.story_en: DOM + INANT — the dominant one is like the lord of the domain (DOM), always in charge.
mnemonic.story_zh: 主宰（DOMINANT）的人就像領地（DOM）的主人——掌控全局，無人能及。

example: English is the dominant language in global business.

definition: to completely remove or get rid of something

mnemonic.story_en: E + LEMON + ATE — we ate the lemon and eliminated the sour taste completely from the recipe.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把檸檬（LEMON）吃掉（ATE），完全消除（ELIMINATE）食譜裡的酸味——送出門檻之外。

example: The goal is to eliminate poverty worldwide.

definition: to come out or become known from a hidden state

mnemonic.story_en: E + MERGE — after a merger, a new company emerges from two, coming out of the process.
mnemonic.story_zh: 合併（MERGE）之後，一家新公司從中浮現（EMERGE）出來——從水中升上水面。

example: A new leader emerged from the crisis.

definition: special importance or prominence given to something

mnemonic.story_en: EM + FACE + IS — emphasis puts a face on what IS most important, showing it in bold.
mnemonic.story_zh: 強調（EMPHASIS）就是把最重要的那張臉（FACE）凸顯出來（EM=放大展示）——讓它最顯眼。

example: The teacher puts emphasis on critical thinking.

definition: to intensify, increase, or further improve quality or value

mnemonic.story_en: EN + HANCE — to enhance is to make something high (haut → hance), lifting its quality up.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「enhance」就是讓某事變高（HANCE = haut = high）——把品質往上（EN）提升。

example: Good lighting can enhance a photograph.

definition: to make certain that something will happen

mnemonic.story_en: EN + SURE — to ensure something is to make sure it is certain. Make it secure.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「ensure」就是讓某件事確定（SURE）——把它變得安全牢固（SECURE）、萬無一失。

example: Please ensure all doors are locked before leaving.

definition: the natural world; the conditions surrounding someone or something
definition_zh: 環境；自然環境；周遭情況

mnemonic.story_en: EN + VIRON + MENT — to be 'environed' is to be surrounded on all sides. Your environment encircles you.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「environment」讓你被四面八方（VIRON）包圍（EN）——周遭的一切就是你的環境。

example: We must protect the environment for future generations.

definition: equal in value, amount, or meaning

mnemonic.story_en: EQUAL + VALENT — equivalent means having equal value. Like two coins worth the same.
mnemonic.story_zh: 等價（EQUIVALENT）就是有相等（EQUI）的價值（VALENT=VALUE）——兩枚硬幣面值一樣。

example: One kilometer is equivalent to 0.62 miles.

definition: to set up or found something on a firm basis

mnemonic.story_en: E + STABLE + ISH — to establish is to make something stable — like building a sturdy stable.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「establish」就是建造一間穩固的馬廄（STABLE）——把某件事牢牢立起來，讓它站穩。

example: The company was established in 1995.

definition: to assess or judge the value or quality of something

mnemonic.story_en: E + VALUE + ATE — to evaluate is to draw out (e) the value and 'eat' through all the details.
mnemonic.story_zh: 評估（EVALUATE）就是把價值（VALUE）掏出來（E）仔細消化（ATE）——看看它到底值多少。

example: The manager evaluates employees every six months.

definition: facts or information indicating whether something is true

mnemonic.story_en: EVIDENT + CE — evidence makes things evident (visible). What you see is the evidence.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「evidence」讓事情變得看得見（EVIDENT）——你所見（VIDERE）就是從中浮出（EX）的證據。

example: The police found evidence at the crime scene.

definition: to develop gradually over time through a process of change

mnemonic.story_en: E + VOLVE — evolution rolls out (VOLVE) from inside, slowly unfurling like a scroll over time.
mnemonic.story_zh: 演化（EVOLVE）就像一卷（VOLVE）捲軸慢慢展開（E）——歷經時間的滾動而逐漸展現。

example: Technology evolves faster every decade.

definition: stated clearly and in detail; leaving nothing implied
definition_zh: 明確的；清楚表達的；露骨的

mnemonic.story_en: EX + PLICIT — explicit unfolds (EX + PLICIT like 'unpleat') everything out clearly, nothing hidden.
mnemonic.story_zh: 明確（EXPLICIT）就是把所有折疊（PLICARE）起來的東西全部攤開（EX）——毫不隱藏。

example: The instructions were explicit and easy to follow.

definition: to make use of unfairly; a bold or daring act

mnemonic.story_en: EX + PLOIT — to exploit is to squeeze out every last profit (ploit sounds like 'pluck') from something.
mnemonic.story_zh: 剝削（EXPLOIT）就是把一切榨（EX）出（PLOIT=摘取）來——把資源或人用到極限。

example: Companies sometimes exploit cheap labor overseas.

definition: an element that contributes to a result or outcome

mnemonic.story_en: FACT + OR — a factor is a doer (FACERE) of facts — something that makes results happen.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「factor」是結果的製造者（FACERE=做）——每個「因素」都在背後做著某件事，促成結果。

example: Diet is a key factor in overall health.

definition: able to bend easily; willing to change or adapt
definition_zh: 有彈性的；靈活的；可變通的

mnemonic.story_en: FLEX + ABLE — a flexible person can flex in any direction. They're able to flex!
mnemonic.story_zh: 有彈性的人（FLEXIBLE）能朝任何方向彎曲（FLEX）——他們具備彎折的能力（ABLE）。

example: She has a flexible schedule and can meet anytime.

definition: the center of attention or activity; to concentrate

mnemonic.story_en: FOCUS = FIRE — the Latin origin is 'hearth'. Everything centers around the fire. That's your focus.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「focus」源自拉丁文的「爐火」（hearth）——一家人圍著火（🔥）坐，那就是焦點所在。

example: Please focus on your work during class.

definition: the underlying basis for something; a structure's base

mnemonic.story_en: FOUND + ATION — what was found at the bottom (fundo) becomes the foundation of everything built above.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在底部（FUND）發現（FOUND）的東西，就成為了上面一切的基礎（FOUNDATION）。

example: Trust is the foundation of every relationship.

definition: the purpose or activity for which something is designed; to operate

mnemonic.story_en: FUN + ACTION — a function is a fun action — every machine's job is like its fun thing to do.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「function」是「FUN + ACTION」——每個機器都有它「好玩的動作」，那就是它的功能。

example: The main function of the heart is to pump blood.

definition: forming a necessary base or core; of central importance

mnemonic.story_en: FUND + AMENTAL — fundamental knowledge is the fund (capital) your mind runs on. It's the base investment.
mnemonic.story_zh: 基礎知識（FUNDAMENTAL）就是你腦子裡的基金（FUND）——是支撐一切的底部投資。

example: Reading is a fundamental skill for all students.

definition: to produce or create something

mnemonic.story_en: GENE + RATE — a gene generates life by replicating at a certain rate. Birth and creation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 基因（GENE）以一定的速率（RATE）複製——「generate」就是以基因為模板，產生新的生命。

example: Solar panels generate electricity from sunlight.

definition: relating to the whole world; comprehensive
definition_zh: 全球的；全世界的；全面的

mnemonic.story_en: GLOBE + AL — global refers to something that spans the whole globe — every part of the ball.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「global」就是涵蓋整個地球儀（GLOBE）的——覆蓋球體（GLOBUS）每一個角落。

example: Climate change is a global problem.

definition: a proposed explanation made on limited evidence as a starting point

mnemonic.story_en: HYPO + THESIS — a hypothesis is a thesis placed underneath — not yet proven, still below the surface.
mnemonic.story_zh: 假說（HYPOTHESIS）是一個還「放在下面」（HYPO）的論點（THESIS）——尚未浮出水面，有待驗證。

example: The scientist tested her hypothesis with experiments.

definition: to recognize and name someone or something

mnemonic.story_en: ID + ENTITY + FY — to identify is to verify the ID of an entity, confirming it's the same one.
mnemonic.story_zh: 識別（IDENTIFY）就是核對一個實體（ENTITY）的身份證（ID）——確認它跟記錄中是同一個。

example: Can you identify the bird in this picture?

definition: to put a plan or decision into effect

mnemonic.story_en: IMPLE + MENT — to implement is to fill (IMPLE=implere) a plan into the mental space of reality.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「implement」就是把計畫填入（IMPLE=填滿）現實中——讓腦中（MENT）的方案落地執行。

example: The new policy will be implemented next month.

definition: implied though not directly expressed
definition_zh: 含蓄的；隱含的；不言而喻的

mnemonic.story_en: IM + PLICIT — implicit is folded IN — the meaning is tucked inside and never shown directly.
mnemonic.story_zh: 隱含（IMPLICIT）就是把意思折疊（PLICIT）藏在裡面（IM）——不直說，讓人自己領會。

example: There was an implicit agreement between them.

definition: to suggest or indicate something without directly stating it

mnemonic.story_en: IM + PLY — layers of plywood (PLY) imply strength without stating it directly. Meaning is layered inside.
mnemonic.story_zh: 夾板（PLY）一層層疊在裡面（IM）卻不明說——「imply」就是把意思藏在層層之間，讓人自己讀懂。

example: Her silence implied that she disagreed.

definition: to point out or show; to be a sign of

mnemonic.story_en: INDEX + ATE — an index finger points and indicates. You ate your words and now point to the truth.
mnemonic.story_zh: 食指（INDEX finger）指向某處——「indicate」就是用手指出（DICARE）、明確點明某件事。

example: Dark clouds indicate that rain is coming.

definition: the capacity to affect others; to have an effect on

mnemonic.story_en: IN + FLUENCE — influence is something that flows into you (IN + FLUERE), changing you from inside.
mnemonic.story_zh: 影響（INFLUENCE）就是某種東西流進（IN + FLUERE）你體內——從裡面悄悄改變你。

example: Parents have a huge influence on their children.

definition: existing as a natural or permanent quality of something

mnemonic.story_en: IN + HERE + NT — inherent qualities are stuck right in HERE — they're glued inside, can't be removed.
mnemonic.story_zh: 固有（INHERENT）的特質就黏（HAERERE）在裡面（IN HERE）——天生帶來的，去不掉。

example: There is an inherent risk in extreme sports.

definition: the ability to assess and act independently; a new plan
definition_zh: 主動性；自發性；倡議；計畫

mnemonic.story_en: INITIATE + IVE — someone with initiative always initiates — they go in first without waiting.
mnemonic.story_zh: 有主動性（INITIATIVE）的人總是率先踏入（INITIATE）——不等別人下令，自己先行動。

example: She took the initiative to organize the event.

definition: the introduction of new ideas, methods, or products

mnemonic.story_en: INNO + VATION — innovation brings the NEW (NOVUS) into existence. A new nation of ideas.
mnemonic.story_zh: 創新（INNOVATION）就是把「新的」（NOVUS）帶進（IN）現實——建立一個全新概念的國度。

example: Silicon Valley is known for technological innovation.

definition: to combine parts into a whole; to include all groups equally

mnemonic.story_en: INTEGER + ATE — to integrate is to eat (ATE) all the integers until they form one whole number.
mnemonic.story_zh: 整合（INTEGRATE）就是把所有整數（INTEGER）吃進去（ATE）——合而為一，成為完整的整體。

example: We need to integrate the new system with the old one.

definition: to explain the meaning of; to understand in a particular way

mnemonic.story_en: INTER + PRET — a pretzel (PRET) is twisted and bent between (INTER) layers — interpreting twists meaning.
mnemonic.story_zh: 解讀（INTERPRET）就像扭轉的椒鹽捲餅（PRET）——在兩者之間（INTER）找出彎曲中的意義。

example: How do you interpret this poem?

definition: to carry out research or study into something

mnemonic.story_en: INVEST + I + GATE — a detective invests time at the gate, following footprints (vestigia) to investigate.
mnemonic.story_zh: 偵探在大門（GATE）投入（INVEST）時間，追蹤足跡（VESTIGIUM）——這就是「調查」（INVESTIGATE）。

example: Police are investigating the robbery.

definition: to show that something is right or reasonable
definition_zh: 證明…正當；為…辯護；對齊（文字）

mnemonic.story_en: JUST + I + FY — 'just I' defends the action: 'I justify myself because it was JUST (fair).'
mnemonic.story_zh: 「JUST（公平）+ I（我）+ FY（使成為）」——我讓自己的行為變得公正合理，這就是「justify」。

example: Can you justify why you were late?

definition: to keep in good condition; to assert or affirm

mnemonic.story_en: MAIN + TAIN — to maintain is to hold (TAIN = tenere) the main thing steady with both hands.
mnemonic.story_zh: 維持（MAINTAIN）就是用雙手（MANUS）緊握（TENERE）住最重要的那件事（MAIN），讓它不動搖。

example: It's important to maintain a healthy lifestyle.

definition: to handle or control skillfully; to control unfairly

mnemonic.story_en: MANI + PULATE — 'many hands pulling' — to manipulate is to use many handfuls of tricks to control.
mnemonic.story_zh: 很多隻手（MANI=MANUS）在拉扯——「manipulate」就是用手把某人或某事操控、擺佈。

example: He manipulated the data to support his theory.

definition: a system or process by which something happens

mnemonic.story_en: MECHANIC + ISM — a mechanism is what a mechanic understands — the inner workings of a machine.
mnemonic.story_zh: 技工（MECHANIC）最懂的東西——機器（MACHINE）內部的運作方式，就是「mechanism（機制）」。

example: Scientists study the mechanism of the immune system.

definition: to move from one place to another; to move seasonally

mnemonic.story_en: MY + GREAT + RATE — birds migrate at a great rate, flying across continents every season.
mnemonic.story_zh: 候鳥以驚人的速度（GREAT RATE）飛越大陸——這種季節性的大規模移動就是「migrate（遷徙）」。

example: Many birds migrate south for the winter.

definition: to make partial changes to something

mnemonic.story_en: MODE + FY — to modify is to change the mode — adjust the manner (modus) of doing something.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「modify」就是切換模式（MODE）——改變做事的方式（MODUS），讓它變得更合適。

example: We need to modify the plan based on feedback.

definition: the reason for acting or behaving in a particular way

mnemonic.story_en: MOTIVE + ACTION — motivation is a motive that moves you to action. The moving force behind behavior.
mnemonic.story_zh: 動機（MOTIVE）驅使你行動（ACTION）——「motivation」是推著你前進的那股力量（MOVERE=移動）。

example: What is your motivation for studying English?

definition: consisting in or expressing refusal; harmful; less than zero

mnemonic.story_en: NEGATE + IVE — a negative person negates everything. They say no to every possibility.
mnemonic.story_zh: 負面（NEGATIVE）的人不斷否定（NEGATE）一切——每個可能性他們都說「不」。

example: Try to avoid negative thinking.

definition: Existing or available in large quantities; overflowing or rich with resources, typical in agricultural or natural contexts.

mnemonic.story_en: A BUN DANCED on the table because there was an abundant supply of bakery goods.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一個小圓麵包（A BUN DANCED）在桌上跳舞，因為這裡有非常豐富的烘焙食品供應。

example: The region is famous for its abundant natural resources and fertile soil.

definition: To come near or nearer to something or someone in distance or time; a way of dealing with a situation or problem.

mnemonic.story_en: AP(ple) PRO(professional) ROACH — a professional roach will approach the apple carefully.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一隻專業的（PRO）蟑螂（ROACH）正小心翼翼地接近蘋果（AP）。

example: As winter begins to approach, birds start migrating south for warmer weather.

definition: Made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, typically as a copy of something natural.

mnemonic.story_en: ART(ificial) I(ntelligence) FI(sh) CIA(l) — an artificial intelligence fish was built by the CIA.
mnemonic.story_zh: 由情報單位製造的人工（ART）智慧魚（FI-sh），完全是人造的產物。

example: This juice contains no artificial colors or flavors, only organic fruit.

definition: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully, often in a legal debate or an argument for personal rights.

mnemonic.story_en: AS(s) SERT(ain) — you must assert your opinion to make everyone feel certain about it.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你必須用非常確定（SERTain）的態度來斷言你的觀點。

example: The defense attorney continued to assert that his client was completely innocent.

definition: Of undisputed origin; genuine and true, especially used to describe cultural artifacts, food, or historical documents.
definition_zh: 真實的；正宗的；道地的；可靠的

mnemonic.story_en: AUTH(or) ENTIC(e) — an authentic author does not need to entice readers with fake news.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一個真正的（authentic）作者（AUTH）不需要用假新聞來誘騙讀者。

example: The museum confirmed that the painting was an authentic piece by Rembrandt.

definition: Of short duration; concise and using few words, often seen in official meetings or summaries.
definition_zh: 簡短的；短暫的；摘要；簡報

mnemonic.story_en: BRIE(f) F(ast) — eating Brie cheese was a very brief and fast snack during the meeting.
mnemonic.story_zh: 快速（F）吃塊起司，是一次非常短暫（brief）的休息。

example: The manager gave a brief presentation before opening the floor for questions.

definition: A class or division of people or things regarded as having particular shared characteristics, widely used in classification systems.

mnemonic.story_en: CAT EG(g) ORY — putting a cat and an egg into the same category of biological shapes is weird.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把貓（CAT）和蛋（EG-g）分在同一個分組類別（category）裡真的很奇怪。

example: Books are arranged by category, such as fiction, history, and science.

definition: To bring or come to an end; to stop a certain activity or condition permanently or temporarily.

mnemonic.story_en: SEA S(top) — when you reach the sea, all roads must cease and stop.
mnemonic.story_zh: 看到海（SEA）的時候，所有的陸路交通都必須停止（cease）。

example: The government ordered the factory to cease operations due to environmental pollution.

definition: Starting with the earliest and following the order in which they occurred, primarily used in history and timelines.

mnemonic.story_en: CHRONO(time) LOGICAL — arranging historical events by time order is completely logical.
mnemonic.story_zh: 依據時間（CHRONO）發展的邏輯（LOGICAL）來排列，就是按時間順序的。

example: The history professor asked us to arrange the dynasties in chronological order.

definition: To make a statement or situation less confused and more clearly comprehensible, often by giving more details.

mnemonic.story_en: CLARI(clear) FY(make) — to clarify means to make the situation perfectly clear to everyone.
mnemonic.story_zh: 清晰（CLARI）加上做（FY）——把事情做得很清晰，就是澄清與闡明。

example: Could you please clarify your last point? I didn't quite understand the details.

definition: Logical and consistent; forming a unified whole, especially used to evaluate essays, arguments, or speech.
definition_zh: 前後連貫的；有條理的；邏輯通順的

mnemonic.story_en: CO(together) HERE(here) NT — all ideas stick together right here, making the essay coherent.
mnemonic.story_zh: 所有論點一起（CO）黏在（haerere）這裡（HERE），文章就會很有條理、前後連貫。

example: The candidate failed to present a coherent strategy for economic growth.

definition: To occur at the same time or occupy the same relative position; to agree or be identical in opinion.

mnemonic.story_en: CO(together) INSIDE — two events falling together inside the same day coincide.
mnemonic.story_zh: 兩件事同時掉進（cadere）同一個日子裡（CO INSIDE），就是同時發生。

example: Our holiday plans coincide with the annual festival in that historic city.

definition: To begin or start an official event, ceremony, action, or a formal period of time.

mnemonic.story_en: COM(pany) MENCE(men) — all men in the company stand up to commence the annual meeting.
mnemonic.story_zh: 公司（COM）的所有人員就位，準備正式開始（commence）大型典禮。

example: The graduation ceremony is scheduled to commence promptly at nine o'clock.

definition: To give someone something, typically money, in recognition of loss, suffering, or injury; to counter-balance a deficiency.

mnemonic.story_en: COM(pany) PENSE(pence) ATE — the company paid many pence to compensate for the bad service.
mnemonic.story_zh: 公司（COM）拿出大筆便士（PENSE）讓人拿去花，藉此補償客戶的損失。

example: The airline provided free vouchers to compensate passengers for the long delay.

definition: To contribute extra features to someone or something in such a way as to improve or emphasize their qualities; a thing that completes something.

mnemonic.story_en: COMPLE(te) MENT — a nice sauce is a perfect complement to complete the entire meal.
mnemonic.story_zh: 用來完整（COMPLE-te）結合的元素，就是最完美的相配補充物。

example: The red wine was selected specifically to complement the rich flavor of the steak.

definition: A part or element of a larger whole, especially of a machine, electronic device, or a complex scientific system.

mnemonic.story_en: COM(pany) PONENT(put) — all parts are put together by the company to form a computer component.
mnemonic.story_zh: 被放在（ponere）一塊（COM）來組成機器的東西，就是零組件或成分。

example: The engineer checked every electronic component before assembling the final product.

definition: Complete and including all or nearly all elements, aspects, or details of something, such as a report or insurance cover.
definition_zh: 全面的；廣泛的；包羅萬象的

mnemonic.story_en: COMPREHEN(d) SIVE — a comprehensive study helps you comprehend every single detail completely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把所有的東西通通抓過來（prehendere）一起看，就是非常全面的、廣泛的。

example: The university offer a comprehensive training program for new international students.

definition: To admit that something is true or valid after first denying or resisting it; to yield a right or a match.

mnemonic.story_en: CON(test) CEDE(yield) — after losing the election, the politician chose to concede the race.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在對抗（CON）之後決定讓步（CEDE），意味著最終只能勉強承認失敗並讓步。

example: The candidate refused to concede the election until every single vote was counted.

definition: To form a notion or idea of something in the mind; to imagine or formulate a plan; also means to become pregnant.

mnemonic.story_en: CON(cept) CEIVE(take) — to take a new concept into your mind is to conceive a great idea.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把想法完整地吸取（capere）進大腦裡，就是構想或在心中想像。

example: It was difficult to conceive how the ancient architects built these massive pyramids.

definition: Serving to settle an issue or terminate a debate; convincing and leaving no room for doubt or further speculation.
definition_zh: 決定性的；結論性的；確鑿的

mnemonic.story_en: CONCLU(sion) SIVE — once the judge arrives at a conclusion, the evidence is deemed conclusive.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把所有的門徹底關上（claudere），不再留有疑問，這就是決定性、確鑿的。

example: The DNA test provided conclusive evidence that the suspect was at the crime scene.

definition: To organize and carry out an activity, such as an experiment or survey; as a noun, the manner in which a person behaves.
definition_zh: 執行；進行（實驗等）；指揮；行為；舉止

mnemonic.story_en: CON(together) DUCT(tube/lead) — leading people through a proper duct to conduct a scientific test.
mnemonic.story_zh: 引導（ducere）大家聚集在一塊（CON），去執行或主導一項大型活動。

example: The research team will conduct a series of interviews with local residents next week.

definition: Notably large in size, amount, or extent; worthy of attention or respect due to its scale or impact.
definition_zh: 相當大的；相當多的；值得考慮的

mnemonic.story_en: CONSIDER ABLE — a sum of money that is so large you are able to consider buying a mansion.
mnemonic.story_zh: 數量龐大到讓你能夠（ABLE）去認真考慮（CONSIDER）的，就是相當可觀的。

example: The company spent a considerable amount of money on marketing the new software.

definition: To be a part of a whole; to combine or form a whole entity, legal law, or a specific system.

mnemonic.story_en: CON(together) STITUTE(statute/set) — setting up individual statutes together to constitute a constitution.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把各個部分一起（CON）建立（statuere）排列起來，就組成了整體結構。

example: Single-parent families constitute a growing percentage of the urban population.

definition: To severely restrict the scope, activity, or freedom of someone or something; to compel by physical or moral force.

mnemonic.story_en: CON(together) STRAIN — pulling the ropes tightly together puts a strain on the prisoner to constrain him.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把繩子緊緊勒在一塊（stringere），讓人感到無比拉扯（STRAIN），就是限制與束縛。

example: Lack of funding will severely constrain the university's ability to expand research.

definition: To eat, drink, or ingest food; to use up a resource such as fuel, time, or energy completely.
definition_zh: 消耗；花費；吃、喝；（火災）燒毀

mnemonic.story_en: CON(completely) SUME(sum) — to consume is to completely take the whole sum of food or fuel.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把所有的總數（SUME）徹底拿走（sumere）吃光，就是消耗或享用。

example: The large old vehicle tends to consume a massive amount of fuel on highways.

definition: To deny the truth of a statement, especially by asserting the opposite; to be in conflict or inconsistent with.

mnemonic.story_en: CONTRA(against) DICT(speak) — to speak against what someone just said is to contradict them.
mnemonic.story_zh: 對著幹、相反（CONTRA）地說話（dicere），這就是反駁與產生矛盾。

example: The eyewitness accounts contradict the official police report of the accident.

definition: Giving rise or likely to give rise to public disagreement and heated, long-lasting argument and debate.

mnemonic.story_en: CONTRA(against) VERSE(turn) — when opinions turn against each other, the topic becomes highly controversial.
mnemonic.story_zh: 意見朝著相反（contra-）的方向轉（vertere），兩派人僵持不下，這就是非常有爭議的。

example: The government's decision to raise retirement age remains deeply controversial.

definition: To change the form, character, or function of something; as a noun, a person who has changed their religious or political beliefs.

mnemonic.story_en: CON(completely) VERT(turn) — to turn completely around means to convert the warehouse into a loft.
mnemonic.story_zh: 徹底（com-）轉向（vertere）另一個方向或格式，就是轉換與轉變。

example: The factory plans to convert coal-powered machines into solar energy systems.

definition: A period of ten years, frequently used in historical analysis, demographic reports, or cultural studies.

mnemonic.story_en: DECA(ten) DE(day) — think of a decade as a giant block of ten long years of history.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字根 DECA 代表十，用來計算時間就是長達十年的期間。

example: The technology sector has undergone massive changes over the past decade.

definition: To state that one refuses to admit the truth or existence of something; to refuse to give or grant something requested.

mnemonic.story_en: DE NY(New York) — the criminal tried to deny that he was ever in New York during the heist.
mnemonic.story_zh: 大聲地朝對方搖頭說不（negare），徹底否認（deny）做過那件事。

example: The suspect continued to deny all allegations made against him by the police.

definition: To show or represent someone or something by a drawing, painting, or other art form; to portray in words in literature.

mnemonic.story_en: DE(fine) PICT(ure) — to depict a historic scene means to draw a very fine picture of it.
mnemonic.story_zh: 用畫筆（pingere）徹底往下（de-）描摹成一張精緻的圖片（PICTure），就是描繪。

example: The ancient murals depict various epic scenes from traditional mythology.

definition: A thing made or adapted for a particular purpose, especially a piece of mechanical or electronic equipment.

mnemonic.story_en: DE(sign) VICE — an electronic device designed to crush a vice grip automatically.
mnemonic.story_zh: 經過精密、巧妙分開（dividere）設計出來的器具，就是智慧型電子裝置。

example: The engineer invented a small device that tracks water purity in real-time.

definition: To give all or a large part of one's time, money, or energy to a specific person, cause, or activity.

mnemonic.story_en: DE(eeply) VOTE — when you deeply vote for a leader, you devote your time to support them.
mnemonic.story_zh: 莊嚴地下定誓言（vovere）要把自己徹底（de-）交出去，代表終身奉獻於此。

example: The scientist decided to devote her entire career to finding a cure for malaria.

definition: A measurable extent of some kind, such as length, breadth, depth, or height; also refers to an aspect or feature of a situation.
definition_zh: 維度；尺寸；面積；（事物的）面向

mnemonic.story_en: DI(vide) MEN SION — the construction men measured each divided section to check the room's dimension.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把空間分開（dis-）進行仔細測量（metiri），算出來的長寬高就是維度與尺寸。

example: Adding a digital component added a whole new dimension to the art project.

definition: To make or become less; to reduce in size, extent, or importance over a period of time.

mnemonic.story_en: DI(vide) MINI(miniature) SH — dividing resources until they become mini will diminish their value.
mnemonic.story_zh: 運用手段讓一個東西變得超級迷你（MINI/minuere），數量和分量就會不斷減少。

example: The pain began to diminish after the doctor administered the medication.

definition: Careful and circumspect in one's speech or actions, especially in order to avoid causing offense or to gain a tactical advantage.
definition_zh: 謹慎的；考慮周到的；不引人注目的

mnemonic.story_en: DISC(us) REET(secret) — a discreet spy keeps all discussion secret to avoid being caught.
mnemonic.story_zh: 懂得把對話和細節分開（discernere）過濾、不露聲色，說話做事極為謹慎。

example: The diplomat made a discreet inquiry regarding the country's border security.

definition: To make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people; to recognize a small distinction.
definition_zh: 歧視；區別對待；辨別；區分

mnemonic.story_en: DIS(apart) CRIMIN(al) ATE — the police discriminate the criminal from innocent citizens by checking records.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把審判罪名（crimen）跟特定人群分開（dis-）或混為一談，從而造成區分或不公的歧視。

example: It is illegal for employers to discriminate against workers based on their race.

definition: To put something in a prominent place so that it may readily be seen; an onward exhibition of information or artwork.

mnemonic.story_en: DIS(un) PLAY — unfolding the poster so that everyone can see it play out on the big screen display.
mnemonic.story_zh: 解除（dis-）摺疊（plicare）狀態並把它攤開展示，就是陳列與顯示。

example: The department store will display the new fashion line in the front window.

definition: Showing a great deal of variety; very different, composed of distinct elements or qualities within a community or ecology.

mnemonic.story_en: DI(vide) VERSE — turning (vertere) in separate ways (dis-) creates a highly diverse set of paths.
mnemonic.story_zh: 往不同的方向（dis-）轉過去（vertere），形成各種不相同的支流，這就是多樣化的。

example: The university prides itself on having a diverse student body from over eighty nations.

definition: Relating to the running of a home or to family relations; existing or occurring within a specific country and not international.
definition_zh: 家庭的；國內的；馴養的；傭人

mnemonic.story_en: DOM(e) ESTIC — living under the dome of your own house refers to domestic life or domestic flights.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字根 DOMUS 代表家或屋頂，引申為屋簷底下的家庭生活，或是國土內部的國內事務。

example: The government is trying to boost domestic consumption to stimulate economic growth.

definition: Characterized by constant change, activity, or progress; a force that stimulates change or progress within a system.
definition_zh: 動態的；有活力的；強有力的；動力

mnemonic.story_en: DYNA(mite) MIC — a speaker holding a microphone (MIC) with dynamite energy is very dynamic.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字根 DYNAMIS 代表能量（如炸藥 DYNA-mite），用來形容局勢不斷變化、充滿活力力道。

example: The market environment is highly dynamic, requiring companies to adapt quickly.

definition: Achieving maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or expense, especially regarding machinery or time management.

mnemonic.story_en: EF(fect) FIC(tion) IENT — working so fast that creating an entire fiction effect seems efficient.
mnemonic.story_zh: 能夠把潛在效果（facere）完美地激發出來（ex-），花費最少的心力達到最高產出。

example: The company introduced an efficient sorting system to speed up delivery times.

definition: Based on, concerned with, or verifiable by observation or experience rather than theory or pure logic.
definition_zh: 實證的；以經驗、實驗為依據的

mnemonic.story_en: EMP(ire) IRICAL — the ancient empire relied on empirical research of building techniques, not theories.
mnemonic.story_zh: 完全沉浸在（en-）親身實驗（peira）中得到的數據，用來指代科學上的實證與經驗科學。

example: The scientific community requires empirical evidence before accepting a new hypothesis.

definition: To unexpectedly experience or be faced with a difficult obstacle or a person; a casual or unexpected meeting.
definition_zh: 遭遇（問題/危險）；不期而遇；衝突

mnemonic.story_en: EN(ter) COUNTER — as you enter the store counter, you suddenly encounter an old friend.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在往前走的時候突然進入（in-）跟某個事物面對面（contra）的狀態，就是突然遭遇或碰見。

example: During the deep forest hike, they were lucky not to encounter any dangerous predators.

definition: Very large in size, quantity, or extent; exceeding the normal limits of scale or proportion.

mnemonic.story_en: E(x) NORMOUS(normal) — something so huge that it completely breaks out of the normal size limits.
mnemonic.story_zh: 完全超出（ex-）了一般正常、常規的範疇（norma），這就叫做龐大、巨大的。

example: The building project cost an enormous amount of money and took five years to complete.

definition: Plain or obvious; clearly seen or understood by anyone with the facts available.

mnemonic.story_en: EVI(dence) DENT — it is totally evident that a car crash happened when you see a massive dent.
mnemonic.story_zh: 讓人一記眼眸就能看得（videre）清清楚楚（ex-），就是顯而易見、十分明顯的。

example: It was evident from his facial expression that he was extremely upset by the news.

definition: To become or make larger or more extensive, such as a balloon inflating or a business opening new branches.

mnemonic.story_en: EX(out) PAND(a) — the global zoo network wants to expand the habitat for the growing giant panda population.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把緊縮的東西向外（ex-）拉扯鋪開（pandere），使範圍和面積大大擴展或膨脹。

example: The online retailer decided to expand its operations into European markets next spring.

definition: Expert skill or knowledge in a particular field, usually built through years of dedicated work or scientific study.
definition_zh: 專長；專業知識；專門技能

mnemonic.story_en: EXPERT ISE — an expert with years of practice shows incredible expertise when solving structural failures.
mnemonic.story_zh: 由專家（EXPERT）所展現出的最高水準技能與理論底蘊，就是專業知識與專長。

example: The consulting firm is seeking someone with deep technical expertise in cyber security.

definition: To rise and fall irregularly in number or amount, highly characteristic of stock markets, temperatures, or currency values.

mnemonic.story_en: FLU(flu) CTUATE — oil prices fluctuate up and down like a wave when a global flu outbreak hits.
mnemonic.story_zh: 像波浪（fluctus）起伏或水流（fluere）一樣不穩定地晃動，代表市場或數據的頻繁波動。

example: Vegetable prices fluctuate wildly depending on the seasonal weather and crop yields.

definition: A mathematical or chemical rule expressed in symbols; a fixed, reliable method for doing or achieving something.
definition_zh: 公式; 配方; 固定方法

mnemonic.story_en: FORM ULA — a standard form that provides a precise mathematical formula for calculation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 形狀、模式（forma）的小型常態封裝，在科學上指代固定代號與化學配方公式。

example: The mathematician discovered a new formula that calculates prime numbers faster.

definition: A formal promise or assurance that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired if broken.
definition_zh: 保證；擔保；保固期；保證書

mnemonic.story_en: GUARD ANT EE — a guard ant guarantees that the queen will be protected under all situations.
mnemonic.story_zh: 像守衛（GUARD）一樣給出鐵一般的承諾與法律授權，確保產品或權益絕對沒問題。

example: The new washing machine comes with a five-year guarantee against mechanical breakdown.

definition: A system or organization in which people or groups are ranked one above another according to status or authority.

mnemonic.story_en: HIER(sacred) ARCHY(rule) — a church system hierarchy where sacred rules decide who sits at the top.
mnemonic.story_zh: 由神聖權力（hieros）所延續下來的統治（arkhein）架構，後用以指代公司或社會階級體制。

example: In a corporate hierarchy, the CEO sits at the very top level of management authority.

definition: To intentionally refuse to take notice of or acknowledge someone or something; to disregard safety warnings.

mnemonic.story_en: I(n) GNORE(know) — to consciously choose not to know or look at the red warning sign.
mnemonic.story_zh: 採取不知道、不理解（in- + gnotus）的態度，去故意不理睬或忽視眼前的訊息。

example: You cannot simply ignore the warnings if you want to complete the task safely.

definition: To explain or make something clear by using examples, charts, or pictures; to serve as a visual example of a story.

mnemonic.story_en: ILLUS(lumin) TRATE — to shine a powerful light into a complex concept to help people illustrate it.
mnemonic.story_zh: 將光芒與明亮（lustrare）投入（in-）黑暗未知中，藉由圖畫與例子將概念徹底闡明。

example: The professor used a detailed case study to illustrate the economic theory to the class.

definition: A thing that motivates or encourages someone to do something, such as a financial bonus or a tax credit.

mnemonic.story_en: IN CENT IVE — a company putting extra cents into your pocket provides an excellent financial incentive.
mnemonic.story_zh: 本意為吹奏喇叭或唱歌（canere）來鼓舞士氣，現指放入額外的錢（CENT）給予實質誘因與激勵。

example: The government offered a tax incentive to encourage families to buy electric cars.

definition: To take something in or include it as a part of a whole; to combine multiple ingredients, features, or systems into one body.
definition_zh: 納入；併入；合併；成立公司

mnemonic.story_en: IN CORPOR(body) ATE — taking separate elements and making them eat into a single grand corporate body.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把外在的點子或成分，放進（in-）一個主要的實體或身體（corpus）之中，即是融合、併入。

example: The designer decided to incorporate traditional patterns into the modern dress line.

definition: Certain to happen and completely unavoidable, like aging, seasonal change, or economic adjustments.
definition_zh: 不可避免的；必然發生的

mnemonic.story_en: IN EVIT(avoid) ABLE — a historical event that is absolutely not (IN) able to be avoided (EVIT).
mnemonic.story_zh: 利用否定前綴（in-）加上可以被躲開的（evitare），得出絕對無法躲避、必然發生的事。

example: With traffic getting worse daily, expanding the subway system became an inevitable choice.

definition: To make changes in something established, especially by introducing new methods, fresh ideas, or tech products.

mnemonic.story_en: IN NOVA(new) TE — pouring entirely new (novus) structural tech into an old standard corporate system to innovate.
mnemonic.story_zh: 將全新（novus）的血液與創意注入（in-）舊有的框架中，這就是進行大刀闊斧的創新。

example: To stay competitive, technology startup firms must constantly innovate and upgrade algorithms.

definition: The capacity to gain an accurate and deep intuitive understanding of a person or a highly complex situation.

mnemonic.story_en: IN SIGHT — having a brilliant inner sight that lets you see deep inside the core psychology of a market.
mnemonic.story_zh: 擁有一雙能夠直接看穿（sight）到內幕本質（in-）的眼睛，比喻精準敏銳的洞察力。

example: The psychologist's study provides valuable insight into child learning patterns.

definition: To look at something closely and formally, typically to assess its condition, safety, or compliance with official laws.

mnemonic.story_en: IN SPECT(look) — the safety inspector stepped inside the laboratory to look at every machine closely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把視線投射到（in-）事物內層去仔細觀看（specere），代表官方的正式安全巡檢或審查。

example: Customs officials will thoroughly inspect every container arriving at the international port.

definition: An example or single occurrence of something happening; to cite a fact or case as a specific evidence or example.
definition_zh: 例子；實例；場合；舉出...為證

mnemonic.story_en: IN STANCE — look at a football player standing in a specific stance as a perfect instance of good form.
mnemonic.story_zh: 站立（stare）在眼前的具體狀態，引申為可以用來直接說明道理的具體案例或點點滴滴。

example: This is just one isolated instance of computer failure, not a systemic network defect.

definition: The quality of being felt strongly or having a very high degree of strength or force, typically used when describing physical energy, light, emotions, or concentrated effort.

mnemonic.story_en: The runners felt the IN TEN CITY (INTENSITY) heat while training hard for the marathon.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在「十個城市」(IN TEN CITY) 裡頂著烈日狂奔，感受到了極高【強度】的考驗。

example: The storm increased in intensity as it approached the coast, causing widespread power outages.

definition: To communicate with or react to each other, used frequently in social contexts to describe people mixing or in scientific contexts to describe substances changing each other.

mnemonic.story_en: When people INTER (enter) the stage, they ACT together to entertain the audience.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當演員們「進入」(INTER) 舞台開始「演戲」(ACT)，他們就在【互動】了。

example: The teacher used educational games to encourage students to interact more with one another during class.

definition: Being or happening between two records, stages, levels, or groups, often used in education or sports to denote a level between beginner and advanced.

mnemonic.story_en: The INTER (between) MEDI (media/middle) stage ATE up most of our project timeline.
mnemonic.story_zh: 處於「兩者之間」(INTER) 且在「中間」(MEDI) 的【中級】課程最花時間。

example: This textbook is designed for intermediate students who already have a basic understanding of English grammar.

definition: Inside an object, building, or body, or existing within an organization or country rather than outside it.

mnemonic.story_en: The IN TURN ALL (INTERNAL) organs function properly one by one inside the body.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在體「內」(IN)，「輪流」(TURN) 讓「所有」(ALL) 臟器運作，這是【內部】的機制。

example: The company launched an internal investigation to find out how the confidential data was leaked.

definition: A period of time between two events or a space between two objects, commonly used in time management, music, and fitness training.

mnemonic.story_en: Between the INTER (between) WALL (val) spaces, we found a hidden time capsule.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在「牆與牆之間」(INTER-WALL) 留下一段【間隔】，用來通風。

example: The train service runs at regular intervals of fifteen minutes during peak rush hours.

definition: Being an extremely important and basic characteristic of a person or thing that cannot be separated from it.

mnemonic.story_en: The IN TRIN (train) SIC (seek) journey shows that motivation must come from within.
mnemonic.story_zh: 坐「進火車」(IN TRAIN) 裡去「尋找」(SEEK) 自我，發現那是最【內在、固有】的價值。

example: Flexibility and critical thinking are intrinsic parts of a modern liberal arts education.

definition: To put money, effort, or time into something to make a profit or achieve a result, standard in finance and personal growth discussions.

mnemonic.story_en: To INVEST money, you put on an IN VEST (vest) suit to look professional at the bank.
mnemonic.story_zh: 穿著「背心」(VEST) 走「入」(IN) 股市，把錢【投資】進去。

example: Governments need to invest heavily in renewable energy to combat long-term climate change.

definition: To use a law, rule, or power to support your arguments, or to call for help from a higher power like a deity.

mnemonic.story_en: The shaman went IN (into) to VOC (voice/call) out to the ancient spirits.
mnemonic.story_zh: 向「內」(IN) 發出「聲音、呼喊」(VOC)，【祈求】神明保佑，或是【援引】條文。

example: The police decided to invoke an emergency law to restore public order during the riots.

definition: To include someone or something as a necessary part or result of an activity, event, or situation.

mnemonic.story_en: The manager wanted to IN VOLVE (roll) everyone into the new group project.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把大家都「捲入」(VOLVE) 這件事情「裡面」(IN)，代表事情【包含】並【涉及】了所有人。

example: Researching history involves analyzing primary sources as well as reading modern textbooks.

definition: To separate something or someone from other things or people, commonly used in medical, social, or scientific laboratory contexts.

mnemonic.story_en: The ICE LATE (ISOLATE) winter storm left the remote cabin completely cut off.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「冰塊」(ICE) 太「遲」(LATE) 融化，導致這個村莊繼續被【隔離】。

example: Scientists managed to isolate the specific gene responsible for the inherited disease.

definition: An important subject or problem that people are thinking and talking about, or an official publication like a magazine edition.

mnemonic.story_en: The IS SUE (issue) court case became a controversial topic discussed nationwide.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這件「是不是」(IS) 要「起訴」(SUE) 的案子，成了一個社會大【議題】。

example: Climate change remains one of the most critical issues facing global leaders today.

definition: A single thing in a set, group, list, or collection, typically used during shopping, inventory taking, or listing tasks.

mnemonic.story_en: The I TEAM (ITEM) checked off every single product on the warehouse list.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「我」(I) 帶領「團隊」(TEAM) 逐一檢查清單上的每一個【品項】。

example: The sales receipt lists each item purchased along with its specific price and tax.

definition: A serious magazine or newspaper that is published regularly, usually about a specialist subject, or a personal diary.

mnemonic.story_en: The JOURNEY ALL (JOURNAL) records were written down daily in his academic notebook.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把「旅程中的所有事」(JOURNEY ALL) 每天記錄下來，就成了個人的【日誌】或學術【期刊】。

example: She published her groundbreaking research on quantum physics in a prestigious scientific journal.

definition: A piece of paper or other material that gives information about the object it is fixed to, or a descriptive phrase applied to a person.

mnemonic.story_en: The LAY BELL (LABEL) factory worker pasted tags onto the products before shipping.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把標籤「放好」(LAY) 並按「鈴」(BELL) 出貨，這是包裝工人在貼【標籤】。

example: Always read the warning label on medicine bottles to understand the correct dosage and side effects.

definition: Practical work, especially hard physical work, or the workers in a nation or industry viewed as a collective group.

mnemonic.story_en: The LAY BORE (LABOR) workers found drilling through the hard rock to be exhausting work.
mnemonic.story_zh: 工人們把工具「放好」(LAY) 開始「鑽孔」(BORE)，這需要付出大量的【勞動】。

example: The construction of the great pyramids required years of intense manual labor by thousands of workers.

definition: A quantity or sheet of something that lies over a surface or between other things, used in geology, cooking, and design.

mnemonic.story_en: The LAY ER (LAYER) of bricks was carefully placed by the mason to build the wall.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一層一層「鋪上去」(LAY)，就形成了蛋糕或地質的【層】次。

example: The geologist explained how different layers of rock represent different eras in Earth's history.

definition: A formal talk on a serious subject given to a group of people, especially students at a university.

mnemonic.story_en: The LEC (lecturer) CHER (cheered) when the whole auditorium listened closely to the speech.
mnemonic.story_zh: 教授在台「選讀」(LECT) 文獻給台下的學生聽，這是一場大學【講課】。

example: The professor gave an inspiring lecture on the causes of the industrial revolution.

definition: Connected with the law, or allowed by the official rules and laws of a country.

mnemonic.story_en: The LEG ALL (LEGAL) system applies to everyone equally within the country.
mnemonic.story_zh: 法律規定「所有人」(ALL) 的「腿」(LEG) 都不能跨越紅線，這樣做才【合法】。

example: You should seek professional legal advice before signing a contract to buy property.

definition: To make or enact laws, a term heavily used in political science and governance contexts.

mnemonic.story_en: The LEDGE IS LATE (LEGISLATE) because congress spent hours debating the new bill.
mnemonic.story_zh: 國會「法律」(LEGIs) 制定「太遲」(LATE)，因為【立法】過程吵個不停。

example: The government intends to legislate against discrimination in the workplace this year.

definition: To officially demand and collect money, a tax, or a fine from citizens or businesses.

mnemonic.story_en: The LEVY (leave) team wanted to LEVY high taxes on imported luxury goods.
mnemonic.story_zh: 國王「抬高」(LEV) 雙手，向平民【徵收】新的進口稅款。

example: The local council decided to levy a new tax on plastic packaging to fund recycling programs.

definition: Respecting and allowing many different types of beliefs or behavior, or generous in amount; also relates to political ideologies favoring progress.
definition_zh: 自由主義的；慷慨的；開明的

mnemonic.story_en: The LIBER (free) ALL (liberal) citizens enjoy freedom of speech and expression.
mnemonic.story_zh: 主張「所有人」(ALL) 都應該擁有「自由」(LIBER) 的觀念就是【開明、自由的】。

example: Her parents had liberal views and allowed her to choose her own career path.

definition: An official document or ticket that gives you permission to own, do, or use something, such as driving a car or running a business.

mnemonic.story_en: The LI (line) SENSE (LICENSE) checker verified that every driver possessed a valid permit.
mnemonic.story_zh: 警察在路上檢查你「是不是」(LI) 有合乎「常理」(SENSE) 地帶著駕駛【執照】。

example: You need to pass both a written exam and a road test to obtain your driver's license.

definition: In the same way, or in a similar manner, frequently used as a transition word in essays and formal debates.

mnemonic.story_en: If you LIKE the WISE advice, you should act LIKEWISE in your own life.
mnemonic.story_zh: 用「同樣的」(LIKE)「方式」(WISE)，【同樣地】處理接下來發生的問題。

example: Just as the first experiment yielded positive results, the second trial likewise proved successful.

definition: A connection between two pieces of electronic data, or a relationship between two people, things, or ideas.

mnemonic.story_en: The LIN (line) KING (LINK) created a strong connection between the two remote villages.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這條「線」(LIN) 像條項鍊把兩端【連結】在一起。

example: Epidemiologists found a clear link between poor diet and increased heart disease risk.

definition: To find the exact position of somebody or something, or to establish a business or home in a particular place.

mnemonic.story_en: We used a LO (low) CATE (gate) map to LOCATE the hidden entrance to the castle.
mnemonic.story_zh: 根據「地點」(LOC)，我們終於在對的位置【找出】或【設置】了工廠。

example: The rescue team used radar technology to locate the hikers stranded on the mountain.

definition: A particular way of thinking, especially one that is reasonable and based on good judgment and correct scientific/mathematical reasoning.

mnemonic.story_en: The LOG IC (LOGIC) system processed data using strict mathematical rules.
mnemonic.story_zh: 寫「程式日誌」(LOG) 時「看電腦」(IC)，每一步都要符合【邏輯】。

example: There is no logic in spending all your money on items you do not actually need.

definition: The empty space to the side of the text on a page, or the difference between what it costs to buy or make something and the price it is sold for.

mnemonic.story_en: The MAR (market) GIN (drink) sellers noted down profits in the narrow MARGIN of the book.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在「火星」(MAR) 上喝「琴酒」(GIN)，只能躲在防護罩的【邊緣】與【空白處】。

example: She wrote brief explanatory notes in the margin of her history textbook during the lecture.

definition: Fully grown or developed physically, mentally, or emotionally, behaving in a sensible, adult way.

mnemonic.story_en: The MA (mother) TOUR (MATURE) guide handled the sudden travel problem with a very calm attitude.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「媽媽」(MA) 帶「旅行團」(TOUR)，處事態度非常【成熟】老練。

example: He showed a very mature attitude when handling constructive criticism from his boss.

definition: To make something as great or large as possible, or to make the best possible use of a resource or opportunity.

mnemonic.story_en: To MAX I MIZE (MAXIMIZE) space, I packed all my heavy clothing in vacuum bags.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把「最大值」(MAX) 當作目標，【使最大化】並充分利用空間。

example: The company adjusted its advertising strategy to maximize quarterly sales and profits.

definition: The internet, newspapers, magazines, television, and radio, considered as a collective group that provides news and information.

mnemonic.story_en: The ME DIA (MEDIA) industry focuses heavily on broadcast news and social networks.
mnemonic.story_zh: 站在中間作為資訊「媒介」(MEDI) 的行業，就是大眾【媒體】。

example: The news media played a critical role in bringing the political scandal to light.

definition: Relating to the science or practice of medicine, or to the treatment of illness and injury without performing surgery.

mnemonic.story_en: The MEDI CAL (MEDICAL) clinic offered free checkups to the entire local community.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「醫生藥物」(MED) 加上「計算大卡」(CAL)，都是關於健康和【醫療的】事。

example: She is planning to pursue a medical degree after finishing her undergraduate studies in biology.

definition: A method or way of expressing something, a substance through which something else flows, or a middle state between two extremes.

mnemonic.story_en: The MEDI UM (MEDIUM) size shirt fits perfectly between small and large sizes.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「中間」(MEDI) 的規格，可以指【中等的】衣服，也可以指傳播資訊的【媒介】。

example: Water is an excellent medium for conducting sound waves over long distances.

definition: Relating to the mind, or involving the process of thinking rather than physical actions.

mnemonic.story_en: The MEN TALL (MENTAL) challenge required immense focus and concentration to solve.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「男人們」(MEN) 想長得「高」(TALL)，除了身體，【心理】素質也要強大。

example: Regular physical exercise is beneficial for both physical and mental health.

definition: A particular way of doing something, especially a systematic, orderly, or well-established logical plan.

mnemonic.story_en: The METH OD (METHOD) for solving the complex math equation was written on the board.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「每一個人」(METH/每) 都要有「點子」(OD/點) 來完成這個科學【方法】。

example: Scientists developed a new method for water purification that uses solar power.

definition: Relating to the armed forces, soldiers, war, or land defense operations of a country.

mnemonic.story_en: The MILI TARY (MILITARY) base guarded the national border day and night.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「一千個」(MILI) 戰士「去打仗」(TARY)，組成強大的【軍隊】。

example: The government increased its military spending to modernize the national defense system.

definition: Very small in amount or degree, or the least possible amount that is necessary or allowed.

mnemonic.story_en: The MINI MAL (MINIMAL) damage meant the historic building did not need costly repairs.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「迷你」(MINI) 的損害，代表受到影響的程度是【最小的】。

example: The safety improvements were completed with minimal disruption to daily office routines.

definition: To reduce something undesirable to the lowest possible level or amount, or to make something seem less important than it really is.

mnemonic.story_en: To MINI MIZE (MINIMIZE) errors, the team double-checked all scientific measurements.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把缺點縮到「最小」(MINI)，就是【使減到最少】。

example: Drivers can minimize the risk of accidents by strictly obeying speed limits.

definition: The smallest amount or number that is possible, allowed, or required in a given situation.

mnemonic.story_en: The MINI MUM (MINIMUM) age requirement to enter the secure facility is eighteen.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「迷你」(MINI) 的極限，「媽媽」(MUM) 說這是法定的【最低限度】。

example: Applicants must have a minimum of three years of professional work experience.

definition: Having little importance, size, or seriousness, especially when compared with other things of the same type.
definition_zh: 較小的；次要的；未成年的

mnemonic.story_en: The MINOR (miner) accident caused only a small delay on the highway.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「挖礦工」(MINER) 撞到了腳指頭，只是受了點【較小的、次要的】輕傷。

example: He made a few minor adjustments to the essay before submitting it to the professor.

definition: A particular way of operating or doing something, or a specific setting on a machine or computer system.

mnemonic.story_en: The MODEL (MODE) of transportation shifted entirely to eco-friendly electric cars.
mnemonic.story_zh: 調整「模型」(MODEL) 的設定，切換到靜音【模式】。

example: Switching your smartphone to airplane mode prevents it from receiving cellular signals.

definition: To watch, observe, or check a situation carefully over a period of time to discover something or see how it develops.

mnemonic.story_en: The MONI TOR (MONITOR) screen allowed guards to watch the entire building closely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 班長「班代」(MONITOR) 盯著電腦螢幕，正在【監視、監測】班上的秩序。

example: Doctors will monitor the patient's heart rate closely during the medical procedure.

definition: Felt or shared equally by two or more people, or describing a legal/business arrangement beneficial to both parties.

mnemonic.story_en: The MUTE YOU ALL (MUTUAL) agreement was signed silently because everyone agreed perfectly.
mnemonic.story_zh: 兩家公司達成「不說話也懂」(MUTE) 的默契，建立起【相互的】信任。

example: The success of the research partnership was based on mutual respect and open communication.

definition: A large system consisting of many similar parts like lines, wires, computers, or people that are connected to each other.

mnemonic.story_en: The NET WORK (NETWORK) engineer repaired the faulty wires to restore internet access.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一張由「網子」(NET) 和「工作線路」(WORK) 織成的網，就是電腦【網路】。

example: Attending business conferences is an excellent way to expand your professional network.

definition: In spite of what has just been said; however, used frequently to contrast information in academic arguments.

mnemonic.story_en: The test was extremely difficult; NEVER THE LESS (NEVERTHELESS) students passed with high grades.
mnemonic.story_zh: 雖然字面上是「絕不、那、更少」(NEVER-THE-LESS)，但合起來代表【儘管如此】依然做了某事。

example: The weather forecast predicted heavy rain; nevertheless, the outdoor music festival went ahead as planned.

definition: In spite of what has just been mentioned; used as a formal connector to introduce a contrasting but true statement.

mnemonic.story_en: He had very little money; NONE THE LESS (NONETHELESS) he donated generously to charity.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「沒有人」(NONE) 會覺得「這變少」(THE LESS)，因為【儘管如此】他還是完成了任務。

example: The scientific theory remains controversial; nonetheless, it has opened up exciting new fields of research.

definition: Ordinary or expected; conforming to a standard, pattern, or regular type that is common.

mnemonic.story_en: The NORM ALL (NORMAL) procedures were followed during the daily factory inspection.
mnemonic.story_zh: 符合「基準、規範」(NORM) 的「所有事物」(ALL)，就是【正常的】。

example: It is perfectly normal to feel a bit nervous before giving a presentation to a large audience.

definition: A belief or idea about something, often one that is vague, traditional, or incomplete rather than scientifically proven.

mnemonic.story_en: The NO TION (NOTION) of flying cars was popular in twentieth-century science fiction.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這個「想法」被記錄在「筆記」(NOTE) 上，形成了一種普遍的【觀念】。

example: The research directly challenged the outdated notion that intelligence is entirely determined by genetics.

definition: Despite the fact or thing mentioned, used in formal legal, academic, or political documents to create an exception.

mnemonic.story_en: NOT WITH STANDING (NOTWITHSTANDING) the heavy rain, the athletic competition continued until sunset.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字面上是「不隨之站立」(NOT WITH STANDING)，也就是【儘管、無視】困難依然前進。

example: Notwithstanding the high cost of materials, the corporate headquarters was completed on schedule.

definition: Relating to the nucleus of an atom, or using energy released from splitting an atom, as in weapons or power generation.

mnemonic.story_en: The NEW CLEAR (NUCLEAR) energy policy aimed to phase out fossil fuels entirely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 希望研發出「全新且乾淨」(NEW CLEAR) 的能源來代替【核能】。

example: International inspectors visited the facility to ensure the nuclear reactor was being used safely.

definition: Something that you plan to achieve; a specific goal or target in a project, military campaign, or business plan.

mnemonic.story_en: The OBJECT IVE (OBJECTIVE) of the game is to capture the flag from the enemy base.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把「物品、對象」(OBJECT) 拋到前方當作努力追求的【目標】。

example: The primary objective of the marketing campaign is to attract younger customers to the brand.

definition: To get or acquire something, especially through deliberate effort, formal request, or official permission.

mnemonic.story_en: To OB TAIN (OBTAIN) a visa, you must submit your application to the embassy.
mnemonic.story_zh: 努力去「握住」(TAIN) 前方的物品，終於把它【獲得】到手。

example: In order to complete the research, we need to obtain permission to access the national archives.

definition: Easy to see, recognize, or understand; clear to anyone who looks or thinks about it.

mnemonic.story_en: The OB VI US (OBVIOUS) solution to the puzzle was staring us right in the face.
mnemonic.story_zh: 就在「路中央」(VIA) 的正對面，擋在我們面前的事物非常【明顯】。

example: It was obvious from her happy expression that she had passed the difficult interview.

definition: To fill, exist in, or use a space, area, or period of time, or to take control of a country or building by force.

mnemonic.story_en: The OCCUPY (pie) activists held signs and filled the entire city park for days.
mnemonic.story_zh: 用手去「抓取」(CAP)，把這個地方【佔領、佔據】下來。

example: Administrative tasks occupy most of the manager's time during the working week.

definition: To happen or take place, especially unexpectedly or as a specific natural event, or to exist within a particular place.
definition_zh: 發生; 出現; 存在於

mnemonic.story_en: The accident OCCUR (occurred) because the driver failed to stop at the red light.
mnemonic.story_zh: 事情「跑過來」(CURR) 撞上了你，代表事情【發生】了。

example: Earthquakes occur frequently in regions located along tectonic plate boundaries.

definition: Strange, unexpected, or unusual, or describing a number that cannot be divided exactly by two.

mnemonic.story_en: The ODD (old) sound coming from the basement made everyone feel uneasy.
mnemonic.story_zh: 長相「怪異」(ODD) 的三個物品，在數學上是個【奇數】。

example: It is odd that he hasn't called yet, as he is usually very punctual.

definition: To balance the effects of something, or to cancel out a negative value or effect with a positive one.

mnemonic.story_en: The company decided to OFF SET (OFFSET) carbon emissions by planting thousands of trees.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在天平「外」(OFF)「放置」(SET) 東西，用來【抵消】原本的重量。

example: The high cost of buying the new machine was offset by the long-term energy savings it provided.

definition: Continuing to exist, happen, or develop, without pausing or stopping, standard in project updates.

mnemonic.story_en: The ON GOING (ONGOING) investigation aims to uncover the root cause of the system failure.
mnemonic.story_zh: 事情在線「上」(ON) 持續「走」(GOING)，代表它是【進行中的】。

example: There is an ongoing debate among economists regarding the best way to control inflation.

definition: A choice between two or more things, or the right to buy or sell something in financial markets.

mnemonic.story_en: The OPT ION (OPTION) menu on the screen allowed users to customize their preferences.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「選擇、眼神看著」(OPT) 前方的各個分頁，挑選一個最好的【選擇】。

example: Students have the option to study abroad during their third year of university.

definition: To discover your position in relation to your surroundings, or to direct somebody's attention or goals toward something specific.
definition_zh: 使適應；定導向；以……為導向

mnemonic.story_en: The hikers stopped to ORIENT (OR-I-ENT) themselves using a compass and a map.
mnemonic.story_zh: 像太陽從「東方」(ORIENT) 升起一樣，我們要先【定向、導向】找出正確位置。

example: The university holding an induction week to orient new students to the campus layout.

definition: The final result or effect of a process, event, election, or medical trial.

mnemonic.story_en: The OUT COME (OUTCOME) of the medical surgery was highly successful.
mnemonic.story_zh: 事情最終「走出來」(OUT-COME) 的樣子，就是它的【結果】。

example: The final outcome of the election will not be known until all votes are formally counted.

definition: An amount of something produced by a person, machine, factory, or country, or data generated by a computer.

mnemonic.story_en: The OUT PUT (OUTPUT) of the smart factory doubled after installing robotic arms.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把生產完的貨物「放出去」(OUT-PUT)，就是工廠的【產量】或電腦的【輸出】。

example: Industrial output increased significantly following the introduction of automated machinery.

definition: Considering everything or including all parts; general rather than specific, often used in executive summaries.

mnemonic.story_en: The OVER ALL (OVERALL) cost of the vacation included flights, hotels, and food.
mnemonic.story_zh: 涵蓋了「在上方越過」(OVER)「全部」(ALL) 的視野，就是【整體的】面貌。

example: Although individual test scores varied, the overall performance of the class was excellent.
