definition: To cover part of something else by extending over its edge, or to share some of the same responsibilities, times, or characteristics.

mnemonic.story_en: The OVER LAP (OVERLAP) between the two schedules caused a major meeting conflict.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在對方的「膝蓋上面」(OVER-LAP) 又鋪了一層布，這叫【重疊】。

example: The responsibilities of the two departments overlap significantly, causing occasional confusion.

definition: In, from, or to countries that are across the sea or ocean; relating to international trade or travel.

mnemonic.story_en: The OVER SEAS (OVERSEAS) market offered massive growth opportunities for the startup.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「越過」(OVER) 汪洋「大海」(SEAS)，去到了【海外的】市場。

example: The corporation plans to expand its overseas operations by opening a new branch in Tokyo.

definition: A small group of chosen experts who discuss something publicly or judge a competition, or a flat rectangular piece of wood, glass, or metal.
definition_zh: 專門小組；（控制）面板；嵌板

mnemonic.story_en: The PANEL (pan) of judges carefully evaluated each singer's vocal technique.
mnemonic.story_zh: 專家們坐在「控制面板」(PANEL) 前面，組成【專門小組】進行評審。

example: A panel of independent scientists was formed to review the environmental safety reports.

definition: A typical example or model of something, or a distinct set of concepts and thought patterns in a scientific discipline.

mnemonic.story_en: The PARA DIGM (PARADIGM) shifted entirely when the internet changed global retail business.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在「旁邊」(PARA) 做一個「點子挖掘」(DIG-M)，成為科技界學術界的【典範】與【思維模式】。

example: The discovery of quantum mechanics triggered a major paradigm shift in modern physics.

definition: A short part of a text, consisting of at least one sentence, that begins on a new line and deals with a single idea.

mnemonic.story_en: The PARA GRAPH (PARAGRAPH) structure in the essay helped separate different arguments.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在文字「旁邊」(PARA) 畫一條線開始「寫字」(GRAPH)，分出一個個【段落】。

example: Please read the third paragraph on page fifty to find the answer to the question.

definition: Moving or situated in the same direction and always remaining the same distance apart, or happening at the same time in a similar way.
definition_zh: 平行的；同方向的；類似的

mnemonic.story_en: The PARA LLEL (PARALLEL) railway lines stretched out into the distance across the plains.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字中間的「ll」長得就像兩條【平行的】線一樣排在「旁邊」(PARA)。

example: The researchers conducted parallel studies in three different countries to verify their findings.

definition: A fixed limit or set of rules that controls how something should be done, or a variable in math and computer programming.

mnemonic.story_en: The PARA METER (PARAMETER) settings adjusted the resolution of the digital image.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在「旁邊」(PARA) 用「米尺」(METER) 測量出來的數據，就是電腦的【參數】或規定【界限】。

example: We must operate within the strict parameters set by the budget committee.

definition: To take part in an activity, event, meeting, or discussion, actively sharing and contributing with others.

mnemonic.story_en: The PART I CIPATE (PARTICIPATE) group allowed me to share my views openly during class.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在一個「部分」(PART)「拿取」(CIP) 自己的位置，代表【參與】了這場活動。

example: All students are encouraged to participate actively in classroom discussions and debates.

definition: A person or organization you work together with closely in a business, relationship, or joint activity.

mnemonic.story_en: The PART NER (PARTNER) in the law firm handled the corporate finance cases.
mnemonic.story_zh: 分擔「部分」(PART) 工作，跟你綁在一起的「那個人」(NER)，就是【夥伴】。

example: The tech giant teamed up with a local partner to distribute its products in Asia.

definition: Allowing things to happen or accepting what other people do without resisting or taking direct, energetic action.

mnemonic.story_en: The PASS IVE (PASSIVE) student just sat quietly without asking any questions during class.
mnemonic.story_zh: 只想讓時間「流逝」(PASS)，不做任何反抗，這是一種【被動的】態度。

example: Watching television is generally considered a passive form of entertainment.

definition: To notice or become aware of something through the senses, or to understand and interpret a situation in a particular way.

mnemonic.story_en: The PER CEIVE (PERCEIVE) system allowed scientists to detect small changes in temperature.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「徹底地」(PER) 去「抓取」(CEIVE) 訊息，大腦就能【察覺、感知】外在事物。

example: Newborn babies can perceive bright colors long before they can focus on fine details.

definition: For or out of every hundred, used extensively in statistics, economics, math, and general reports.

mnemonic.story_en: The PER CENT (PERCENT) profit increased by ten units after the summer sale.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「每一」(PER)「一百個一分錢」(CENT)，就是【百分之……】的由來。

example: Over eighty percent of the survey respondents expressed high satisfaction with the new product.

definition: A specific length of time characterized by particular events, culture, or conditions, or a single lesson in a school day.

mnemonic.story_en: The PERI OD (PERIOD) of economic growth lasted for more than a golden decade.
mnemonic.story_zh: 繞著圓圈「周圍」(PERI) 走完一段路程，代表度過了一個【時期】。

example: The Renaissance was a period of remarkable artistic and scientific achievement in Europe.

definition: To continue firmly or obstinately in an opinion or a course of action despite difficulty, opposition, or failure.

mnemonic.story_en: The PER SIST (PERSIST) heavy rain threatened to flood the streets if it didn't stop soon.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「始終、徹底地」(PER)「站立著」(SIST) 不肯倒下，代表意志【堅持】或壞天氣【持續存在】。

example: If the painful symptoms persist for more than three days, you should consult a doctor immediately.

definition: A particular way of considering something or an individual point of view, or the artistic technique of depicting depth on a flat surface.

mnemonic.story_en: The PER SPEC TIVE (PERSPECTIVE) drawing accurately showed the long hallway fading into the back.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「透過」(PER) 望遠鏡「看」(SPEC) 過去，能帶給你全新的【觀點】與空間【透視法】。

example: Travel helps broaden your perspective by exposing you to different cultures and ways of life.

definition: A distinct stage in a process of development, change, growth, or a sequence of events, like the changing appearance of the moon.

mnemonic.story_en: The first PHASE (phase) of the engineering project involved clearing the construction site.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這個「階段」要面對(FACE) 不同的挑戰，每一個【階段、時期】都很重要。

example: The clinical trials for the new vaccine are currently entering their final phase.

definition: Something that exists and can be seen, felt, or experienced, especially something unusual, remarkable, or scientifically interesting.
definition_zh: 現象；奇蹟；非凡的人事物

mnemonic.story_en: The PHE NO MEN ON (PHENOMENON) northern lights attracted thousands of tourists to Iceland.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這是一件「非同小可」(PHE-NO-MEN) 且在線「上」(ON) 爆紅的自然【現象】。

example: Glaciers melting rapidly is a clear phenomenon associated with rising global temperatures.

definition: The study of the fundamental nature of knowledge, reality, and existence, or a particular set of beliefs governing individual behavior.

mnemonic.story_en: The PHILO SOPHY (PHILOSOPHY) professor encouraged students to question the meaning of truth.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「喜愛」(PHILO)「智慧」(SOPHIA) 的學問，就是探索宇宙本質的【哲學】。

example: Her management philosophy focuses on empowering individual employees rather than micromanaging them.

definition: Relating to the body rather than the mind, or relating to real material things that can be seen and touched.

mnemonic.story_en: The PHYS IC AL (PHYSICAL) fitness test required running two miles in under fifteen minutes.
mnemonic.story_zh: 大自然「物理性」(PHYS) 的存在，包括我們的【身體】與觸手可及的【物質】。

example: The doctor conducted a thorough physical examination to ensure the athlete was fit to play.

definition: Added to, or with the addition of, used in mathematics or to introduce an extra positive factor or advantage.

mnemonic.story_en: Two PLUS (plus) two equals four, which is a foundational concept in elementary math.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「加」(PLUS) 上更多的東西，符號是個十字架「＋」。

example: The job offers a competitive salary plus an annual performance-based bonus.

definition: A set of ideas or a plan of what to do in particular situations that has been officially agreed to by a group, business, or government.

mnemonic.story_en: The POLI CY (POLICY) guidelines restricted employees from using personal devices for work.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在「城市、政府」(POLI) 治理中制定出來的宏觀【政策】或公司內部規定。

example: The university updated its attendance policy to allow for medical emergencies.

definition: A part or share of something larger, or an amount of food served for one person in a restaurant.

mnemonic.story_en: The PORT ION (PORTION) of the text was quoted directly in the research paper.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在「港口」(PORT) 把貨物分成一袋一袋的【部分】與【份量】送走。

example: She carefully allocated a portion of her monthly salary to her savings account.

definition: To cause a problem, danger, or difficulty, or to sit in a particular position so that someone can photograph or paint you.

mnemonic.story_en: The POSE (pose) for the camera required standing completely still for three minutes.
mnemonic.story_zh: 模特兒「擺好姿勢」(POSE) 的同時，這個難題也對我們【造成】了考驗。

example: Rising sea levels pose a direct and serious threat to low-lying coastal communities.

definition: Full of hope and confidence, or expressing certainty and agreement; in science, denoting a value greater than zero or a medical test showing a disease exists.
definition_zh: 積極的；正面的；確定的；陽性的

mnemonic.story_en: The POSI TIVE (POSITIVE) attitude of the coach motivated the team to win the match.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把目標確實地「放置穩固」(POS)，心態就會變得無比【積極、正面、確定】。

example: The manager provided positive feedback, praising the team's exceptional creativity.

definition: Possible when the necessary conditions exist; capable of developing into something real or successful in the future.
definition_zh: 潛在的；可能的；（n. 潛力）

mnemonic.story_en: The POTEN TIAL (POTENTIAL) energy stored in the dam was converted into electricity.
mnemonic.story_zh: 擁有強大的「力量與威力」(POTENT)，代表未來非常有【潛力與潛在可能】。

example: The marketing team identified college students as potential customers for the new app.

definition: A person who works in a professional job that requires advanced skill and specialized training, such as a doctor or lawyer.
definition_zh: 執業者（尤指醫生或律師）；從業人員

mnemonic.story_en: The PRACTI TIONER (PRACTITIONER) opened a private clinic after years of hospital service.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把理論付諸「實踐、練習」(PRACTICE) 的專業人員，就是【執業者】。

example: She consulted a qualified medical practitioner before starting the alternative therapy.

definition: To happen, come, or go before something or someone else in time, order, or position.

mnemonic.story_en: The PRE CEDE (PRECEDE) chapters explained the historical background of the revolution.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在「前面」(PRE)「走過來」(CEDE)，代表這件事【在……之前發生】。

example: A brief musical introduction will precede the president's formal address.

definition: Exact and accurate, paying severe attention to details, standard in mathematics, engineering, and scientific measurements.

mnemonic.story_en: The PRE CISE (PRECISE) laser tool cut the diamond with perfect accuracy.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在「前面」(PRE) 先把它「切乾淨」(CISE)，切口就會非常【精確、準確】。

example: The laboratory technician recorded the precise weight of the chemical sample.

definition: To say that an event or action will happen in the future, often based on scientific data, observation, or calculation.

mnemonic.story_en: The PRE DICT (PREDICT) system analyzed market trends to forecast stock prices.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在事情發生「之前」(PRE) 先「說出來」(DICT)，這就是【預測】。

example: Meteorologists use complex satellite models to predict the pathway of tropical storms.

definition: Being the most common, powerful, important, or noticeable feature or group within a particular situation.
definition_zh: 佔主導地位的；顯著的；最主要的

mnemonic.story_en: The PRE DOMINANT (PREDOMINANT) language spoken in this region is Spanish.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在「前方」(PRE) 展現出「統治支配地位的」(DOMINANT)，代表它是【最主要的、主導的】。

example: Pine trees are the predominant species in the northern forest ecosystem.

definition: Coming before a more important action or event, especially as an essential introductory step or preparation.

mnemonic.story_en: The PRE LIMINARY (PRELIMINARY) hearing was held to determine if there was enough evidence for a trial.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在跨進「門檻」(LIMIN)「之前」(PRE) 做的事情，都是【初步的、預備的】。

example: The committee released a preliminary report before finalizing the comprehensive plan.

definition: To believe something to be true because it is highly likely or probable, although you are not completely certain.

mnemonic.story_en: The PRE SUME (PRESUME) concept meant the missing keys were probably left in the car.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在沒有證據「之前」(PRE) 先「拿取、抱持」(SUME) 某個想法，這叫做【假定、推定】。

example: In legal systems, a suspect is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

definition: Happening or existing before something else or before the specific time currently being discussed.

mnemonic.story_en: The PRE VI OUS (PREVIOUS) owner of the historic house maintained the garden beautifully.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在同一條「道路」(VIA)「之前」(PRE) 出現的人事物，就是【先前的】。

example: Applicants must demonstrate relevance by describing their previous work experience.

definition: More important than anything else; chief, main, or relating to the earliest stage of development or education.

mnemonic.story_en: The PRI MARY (PRIMARY) objective of our health campaign is to reduce sugar intake.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「第一、最初」(PRIM) 的位置，延伸出【首要的、主要的】重要性。

example: The primary concern of the rescue team was finding shelter for the stranded passengers.

definition: Of the best possible quality, or excellent; in mathematics, describing a number that can only be divided by itself and one.
definition_zh: 最優良的；主要的；（n. 精華期；質數）

mnemonic.story_en: The PRIME (prime) minister delivered a speech regarding national security.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「最頂級、第一」(PRIME) 的位置，就是人生的【精華期】或最【主要的】地段。

example: This downtown location is a prime example of high-value commercial real estate.

definition: First in order of importance; main, or the person in charge of a school or college.
definition_zh: 主要的；首要的；（n. 校長；本金）

mnemonic.story_en: The PRINCI PAL (PRINCIPAL) reason for the delay was a sudden IT network failure.
mnemonic.story_zh: 學校裡「第一重要的人」(PRINCI) 就是【校長】，他決定了【主要的】政策。

example: The principal ingredient in this traditional Italian dish is fresh tomatoes.

definition: A basic truth, law, rule, or assumption that forms the foundation for a scientific theory, belief system, or moral code.

mnemonic.story_en: The PRINCI PLE (PRINCIPLE) of free speech is protected under the constitution.
mnemonic.story_zh: 事物「最初、源頭」(PRINCI) 的準則，就是科學的【原理】或做人的【原則】。

example: He refused to compromise his moral principles even when facing severe political pressure.

definition: Existing or happening before something else in time, or taking precedence in order of importance.
definition_zh: 先前的；在先的；更重要的

mnemonic.story_en: The PRIOR (prior) notice allowed the tenants to pack their belongings comfortably.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在事情「前面、先拉出來」(PRI)，這件事情是【先前的】，享有【優先權】。

example: The aircraft was unable to land due to a prior emergency on the main runway.

definition: A special right, advantage, or immunity granted only to a particular person or group, often within social or legal contexts.

mnemonic.story_en: A PRIV-ate LEGE-islature grants special rights to a selected few, creating exclusive benefits.
mnemonic.story_zh: 私人的（PRIV）法律（LEGE）只為少數人服務，這就是一種「特權」。

example: Higher education should be a universal right rather than a privilege for the wealthy.

definition: An established or official way of doing something, typically a series of steps taken in a specific order.

mnemonic.story_en: To PRO-ceed is to go forward, and a PRO-CED-ure is the formal way you go forward step by step.
mnemonic.story_zh: 向前（PRO）走（CED）的常規路線，指的就是辦事的「程序」。

example: The laboratory has strict safety procedures that all researchers must follow.

definition: To begin or continue a course of action, or to move forward after a brief interruption.

mnemonic.story_en: When the light turns green, you PRO-ceed and move CEED-forward on your journey.
mnemonic.story_zh: 朝著前面（PRO）走（CEED）去，代表活動「繼續進行」。

example: After addressing the initial questions, the speaker proceeded with her presentation.

definition: A series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular end or result.

mnemonic.story_en: A PRO-cess is a continuous movement where steps go CESS-forward toward a goal.
mnemonic.story_zh: 事物向前（PRO）發展演進的走（CESS）向，就是「過程」。

example: Learning a new language is a slow process that requires daily dedication.

definition: Relating to or belonging to a profession, exhibiting a high standard of skill and behavior appropriate to a career.

mnemonic.story_en: A PRO-fessional is someone who publicly FESS-confesses or declares expertise in a career.
mnemonic.story_zh: 公開（PRO）宣稱（FESS）自己具備某種專長的人，表現就很「專業」。

example: He maintained a strictly professional relationship with his business partners.

definition: To formally forbid something by law, rule, or other authority, preventing it from happening.

mnemonic.story_en: To PRO-hibit is to hold someone HIBIT-away from doing what they want.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在面前（PRO）把人扣留住（HIBIT）不讓過去，就是「禁止」。

example: The school regulations strictly prohibit the use of mobile phones during exams.

definition: An individual or collaborative enterprise that is carefully planned to achieve a particular aim.

mnemonic.story_en: You PRO-ject your ideas forward by JECT-throwing them into a concrete plan.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把想法往前（PRO）扔（JECT）出去並付諸實行，就成了一個「計畫」。

example: The government launched a major research project to study renewable energy sources.

definition: To support or encourage the progress or growth of something, or to raise someone to a higher position.

mnemonic.story_en: To PRO-mote a product or worker is to MOTE-move them forward into a better status.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把位置往前（PRO）移（MOTE），代表「提升」或「促進」。

example: The campaign aims to promote healthy eating habits among young children.

definition: A part, share, or number considered in comparative relation to a whole.

mnemonic.story_en: Dividing assets PRO-equally according to each person's PORTION-share ensures fairness.
mnemonic.story_zh: 按照（PRO）各自應得的份額（PORTION）分配，指的就是「比例」。

example: A large proportion of the company's profits is reinvested in research.

definition: The possibility or likelihood of some future event occurring, or an outlook for the future.

mnemonic.story_en: You look PRO-forward with your SPECT-eyes to see what the future holds.
mnemonic.story_zh: 向前（PRO）看（SPECT），預測未來的動向，就是「前景」。

example: The job offer improved his long-term career prospects significantly.

definition: The official system of rules governing affairs of state, diplomatic occasions, or scientific experiments.
definition_zh: 協定；草案；禮儀；協定規範

mnemonic.story_en: The PROTO-first rule is glued to the front of the book to establish the official standard.
mnemonic.story_zh: 最前面（PROTO）黏著（kolla）的草稿頁，演變為官方的「協定」或「禮儀」。

example: The researchers followed a strict medical protocol to test the new vaccine safely.

definition: The scientific study of the human mind and its functions, especially those affecting behavior in a given context.

mnemonic.story_en: PSYCHO-logy is the LOGY-study of the human soul and mind.
mnemonic.story_zh: 關於心智靈魂（PSYCHO）的研究學問（LOGY），即「心理學」。

example: Understanding consumer psychology can help businesses design better marketing campaigns.

definition: The act of making information, a book, or a journal available to the general public.

mnemonic.story_en: A PUB-lication takes private writing and makes it available to the general PUB-lic.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把內容公開給公眾（PUB），這個動作就是「出版」。

example: The scientific journal delayed the publication of the article for further review.

definition: To prepare and issue a book, journal, piece of music, or information for public sale or distribution.

mnemonic.story_en: To PUB-lish means to take a private document and share it openly with the PUB-lic.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把私人的文字釋出給社會大眾（PUB），意為「發表」或「出版」。

example: The research team hopes to publish their findings in a prestigious medical journal next month.

definition: To acquire something by paying money for it; to buy goods or services.

mnemonic.story_en: You CHASE-after a product and push PUR-forward with money to secure the ownership.
mnemonic.story_zh: 拼命追逐（CHASE）自己想要的東西，最後掏錢將其買下，即「購買」。

example: Tickets for the concert can be purchased online starting tomorrow morning.

definition: To follow someone or something in order to catch or attain them, or to engage in an activity over a long period.

mnemonic.story_en: To PUR-sue a dream means to follow your goals and run SUE-forward without giving up.
mnemonic.story_zh: 向前（PUR）緊緊跟隨（SUE/sequi）夢想，就是「追求」。

example: She decided to pursue a degree in international relations at a top university.

definition: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quality of something rather than its numerical quantity.
definition_zh: 質化的；定性的；性質上的

mnemonic.story_en: QUALIT-ative research focuses on the intrinsic QUALIT-y and characteristics, not numbers.
mnemonic.story_zh: 著重於事物的本質與品質（QUALITY）而非數量的研究，稱為「質化的」。

example: The sociologists used qualitative methods, such as deep interviews, to gather rich data.

definition: To repeat or copy words from a source, typically with an acknowledgment of the original author.

mnemonic.story_en: To QUOTE was originally to mark chapters by QUOT-how many numbers they had.
mnemonic.story_zh: 原本是指標註章節的數目（QUOT），後來演變為指出他人說過話的「引用」。

example: The journalist decided to quote the prime minister's speech verbatim in the article.

definition: Relating to or affecting the fundamental nature of something; far-reaching, thorough, or extreme.

mnemonic.story_en: A RADIC-al change goes straight to the RADIC-root of the problem, tearing it up fully.
mnemonic.story_zh: 從植物的根部（RADIC）發生的變化，是非常「徹底的」或「激進的」。

example: The new manager proposed a radical overhaul of the company's outdated structure.

definition: Made, done, or happening without method or conscious decision; lacking a predictable pattern.

mnemonic.story_en: Like a wild river running at full RAND-speed, things happen without a set path or order.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自法語河流的湍急奔流（RANDUN），毫無既定規則，演變為「隨機的」。

example: The scientists selected a random sample of citizens to take part in the health survey.

definition: The area or extent covered by or included in something; the limits between which variation is possible.

mnemonic.story_en: Objects are placed in a long RANG-row, defining the total distance or scope covered.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一整排（RANC）拉開的距離，就形成了一個可變動的「範圍」。

example: The hotel offers a wide range of facilities, including a spa and a gym.

definition: The quantitative relation between two amounts showing the number of times one value contains or is contained within the other.

mnemonic.story_en: You use your RATIO-rational mind to calculate the mathematical relationship between numbers.
mnemonic.story_zh: 用理性思維來算（RATIO）兩個數目之間的倍數關係，就是「比例」。

example: The ratio of male to female students in the engineering department is three to one.

definition: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic, rather than emotions or superstition.
definition_zh: 理性的；合理的；神智清醒的

mnemonic.story_en: A RATION-al person relies on careful RATION-calculation and clear logic before making a choice.
mnemonic.story_zh: 做事講求依據與計算（RATIO），不感情用事，即為「理性的」。

example: We need to have a rational discussion about the budget instead of arguing blindly.

definition: To act in response to something; to respond to a stimulus, situation, or chemical substance.
definition_zh: 反應；做出反應；起化學反應

mnemonic.story_en: When an event occurs, you ACT-back in RE-sponse to what just happened.
mnemonic.story_zh: 對方做了一個動作，你再做動作回（RE）應（ACT）過去，就是「反應」。

example: Investors reacted quickly to the news, causing the stock market to drop.

definition: A person who rises in opposition or armed resistance against an established government or ruler.

mnemonic.story_en: A RE-bel is someone who wages BELL-war back against the authorities.
mnemonic.story_zh: 再次（RE）發動戰爭（BELL）對抗統治者的人，就是「反叛者」。

example: The rebel groups gained control of several key cities in the northern region.

definition: To move back or further away from a previous position, or to gradually diminish.

mnemonic.story_en: As the floodwaters RE-cede, they CEDE-go back into the river channels.
mnemonic.story_zh: 腳步往回（RE）走（CEDE），通常用來形容洪水或髮際線「後退」。

example: The floodwaters began to recede after three days of continuous sunshine.

definition: A period of temporary economic decline during which trade and industrial activity are reduced.

mnemonic.story_en: An economic RE-cession is a period where market growth goes CESS-backward instead of moving forward.
mnemonic.story_zh: 市場經濟往回（RE）走（CESS），代表景氣進入「衰退」期。

example: Many small businesses closed down during the global economic recession.

definition: A set of instructions for preparing a particular dish, including a list of the ingredients required.

mnemonic.story_en: A RECIPE originally meant take this medicine, instructing how to REC-receive and mix ingredients.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字根意為拿取（RECIPERE），最早是醫生開給病人拿藥的單子，後演變為「食譜」。

example: She followed her grandmother's secret recipe to make the traditional chocolate cake.

definition: The action or process of recognizing or being recognized, or appreciation for an achievement.

mnemonic.story_en: When you see someone, you COGN-know them RE-again, which triggers immediate recognition.
mnemonic.story_zh: 再次（RE）知道（COGN）並想起來對方的身份，就是「認出」或「承認」。

example: The company gave him an award in recognition of his thirty years of loyal service.

definition: To return to a normal state of health, mind, or strength, or to find and regain possession of something lost.

mnemonic.story_en: After losing your energy, you COVER-hide the gaps and get your strength RE-back again.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把失去的原氣重新找回（RE），將身體的虛弱給蓋（COVER）過去，即「康復」。

example: It took him several weeks to fully recover from the severe chest infection.

definition: To enlist someone in the armed forces or to enroll new members into an organization or society.

mnemonic.story_en: To RE-recruit is to make your company's workforce CRUIT-grow bigger by adding new people.
mnemonic.story_zh: 讓團隊的規模再次（RE）擴大生長（CRUIT/crescere），所以需要「招募」新人。

example: The tech firm is looking to recruit fresh graduates for its software engineering team.

definition: The action of mentioning or alluding to something, or a source of information used to check facts.

mnemonic.story_en: You FER-carry your attention RE-back to an original text to confirm a specific fact.
mnemonic.story_zh: 寫論文時，把觀點帶回（RE）到前人的文獻（FER）中去尋求支持，稱為「參考」。

example: The author included a complete list of academic references at the end of the chapter.

definition: To remove impurities or unwanted elements from a substance, or to improve something by making small adjustments.

mnemonic.story_en: You process a material RE-again and again until it becomes perfectly FINE-delicate and pure.
mnemonic.story_zh: 重複（RE）加工直到事物變得極其精細（FINE），就是「提煉」或「改善」。

example: Engineers are working hard to refine the software before its official market release.

definition: To throw back heat, light, or sound without absorbing it, or to think deeply about a specific topic.

mnemonic.story_en: Light hits a mirror and FLECT-bends RE-back into the room, creating an image.
mnemonic.story_zh: 光線折射彎曲（FLECT）並彈回（RE）來，這是「反射」，引申為大腦「深思」。

example: The smooth surface of the lake reflected the majestic snow-capped mountains.

definition: To make changes in something, typically a social, political, or economic institution, in order to improve it.

mnemonic.story_en: To RE-reform a broken system is to give it a completely new FORM-shape for improvement.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把不好的體制打破，重新（RE）塑造形體（FORM），這就是「改革」。

example: The government promised to reform the educational system to reduce student stress.

definition: A condition of being safe or sheltered from pursuit, danger, or serious trouble.

mnemonic.story_en: When danger strikes, you FUG-flee RE-back to a safe place where nobody can hurt you.
mnemonic.story_zh: 往後面（RE）逃跑（FUG）以躲避危險，那個安全的地方就是「避難所」。

example: The small mountain village provided a safe refuge for people fleeing the war.

definition: To indicate that one is not willing to accept, grant, or do something requested.

mnemonic.story_en: When someone offers you food you dislike, you FUSE-pour it RE-back into their container.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把別人遞過來的東西往回（RE）倒（FUSE）過去，表示「拒絕」接受。

example: The local council refused to grant permission for the new shopping mall project.

definition: A government, especially an authoritarian one, or a system or ordered way of doing things.

mnemonic.story_en: A REG-ime is a strict system maintained by those who REG-rule a country with power.
mnemonic.story_zh: 由統治者（REG）所建立起來的國家控制體系，即為「政權」。

example: The old military regime was overthrown following months of public protests.

definition: An area or division, especially part of a country or the world having definable characteristics.

mnemonic.story_en: A REG-ion was originally a distinct territory managed and boundaries fixed by a REG-ruler.
mnemonic.story_zh: 由一位統治者（REG）所管轄的土地邊界，也就是一個「地區」。

example: The tropical region of the country is famous for producing high-quality coffee beans.

definition: To enter or record an official name or fact in a list, book, or financial log.

mnemonic.story_en: To REGISTER is to bring GER-data back RE-into an official records book for tracking.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把個人的資料往回帶（GER/gerere）並寫入系統庫（RE）中，就是「註冊」。

example: Students must register for their elective classes before the end of the week.

definition: To control or maintain the rate or speed of a machine or process so that it operates properly.

mnemonic.story_en: To REG-regulate traffic is to use strict REG-rules to control how fast cars move safely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 利用既定的規則（REGULA）來管轄與約束行為，稱為「管制」或「調節」。

example: The government set up an agency to regulate the prices of basic food items.

definition: A rule or directive made and maintained by an authority to manage behavior or processes.

mnemonic.story_en: REG-ulations are the written REG-rules that citizens must obey to keep social order.
mnemonic.story_zh: 為了維持秩序，官方所頒布的條理與規則（REGULA），即「規章」。

example: The safety regulations require all factory workers to wear hard hats.

definition: To strengthen or support an object, idea, or army, especially with additional personnel or material.

mnemonic.story_en: To RE-inforce a wall is to build inner IN-strength FORCE-again so it never collapses.
mnemonic.story_zh: 再次（RE）投入（IN）力量與強度（FORCE），使其更加穩固，即「加強」。

example: The teacher used interactive games to reinforce the new vocabulary learned in class.

definition: To refuse to accept, submit to, believe, or make use of an idea, gift, or proposal.

mnemonic.story_en: When a proposal is bad, the committee decided to JECT-throw it RE-back to the writer.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把別人送上來的東西毫不留情地往回（RE）扔（JECT），這就是「拒絕」。

example: The university committee voted to reject the proposal due to lack of funding.

definition: To make or become less tense, tight, or anxious; to rest from work or effort.

mnemonic.story_en: After a hard day, you loosen up and bring your body RE-back to a LAX-loose, peaceful state.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把緊繃的身體狀態往回拉（RE），使其恢復鬆弛（LAX），就是「放鬆」。

example: Listening to classical music helps me relax after a long, stressful day at work.

definition: To allow or enable to escape from confinement; to set free or make available to the public.

mnemonic.story_en: To RELEASE a prisoner is to loosen LEASE-the chains and let them go RE-back home.
mnemonic.story_zh: 鬆開束縛（LAX/LEASE）並讓其返回（RE）自由，意為「釋放」或「發布」。

example: The prison officials decided to release the inmate early for good behavior.

definition: Closely connected or appropriate to what is being done or considered at the time.
definition_zh: 相關的；切題的；有重大關係的

mnemonic.story_en: You LEV-raise up a piece of evidence RE-again because it is helpful and fits the topic perfectly.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在討論中再次（RE）被舉起（LEV）作證的重要訊息，必定是與主題「相關的」。

example: Please include all relevant experience on your resume when applying for the job.

definition: A feeling of reassurance and relaxation following the release from anxiety or distress.
definition_zh: 解脫；寬慰；（痛苦的）減輕；救濟物資

mnemonic.story_en: When a problem is solved, a heavy burden is LIEF-raised up and taken RE-away from your back.
mnemonic.story_zh: 壓在心頭的重擔被重新（RE）舉起並挪走（LEV），讓人感到無比「寬慰」。

example: It was a huge relief to hear that everyone survived the earthquake safely.

definition: To depend on with full trust or confidence for support or practical help.

mnemonic.story_en: To RELY on a friend means you are tightly LY-bound to them for mutual trust.
mnemonic.story_zh: 命運與信任和對方緊緊綁（LY/ligare）在了一起（RE），就是「依靠」。

example: As an independent project, we rely heavily on volunteers to complete the work.

definition: To take something away from the position it occupies; to eliminate or eliminate a barrier.

mnemonic.story_en: To REMOVE garbage is to MOVE-move it RE-away from your clean living space.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把不屬於這裡的東西往外（RE）移走（MOVE），也就是「移除」。

example: You need to remove your shoes before entering the traditional Japanese restaurant.

definition: To need something for a particular purpose, or to make something mandatory under rules or laws.

mnemonic.story_en: The boss will QUIRE-ask for the report RE-again and again because it is urgently needed.
mnemonic.story_zh: 反覆（RE）向你尋求與索取（QUIRE）某物，說明這個任務極其「需要」。

example: Most professional jobs require candidates to have at least a bachelor's degree.

definition: A thing that is compulsory; a necessary condition or quality that must be fulfilled.

mnemonic.story_en: A REQUIRE-ment is an essential asset that a university QUIRE-seeks from applicants before entry.
mnemonic.story_zh: 學校依規定強力尋求（QUIRE）你具備的能力，這就是入學的「必要條件」。

example: Meeting the English proficiency requirement is essential for international applicants.

definition: The systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources in order to establish facts and reach new conclusions.

mnemonic.story_en: Scientists SEARCH-look for hidden answers RE-again and again until they find the truth.
mnemonic.story_zh: 為了尋求真理而反覆（RE）尋找（SEARCH）答案的過程，即是學術「研究」。

example: Medical research has led to significant breakthroughs in cancer treatment.

definition: To have one's permanent home in a particular place, or to exist within a specific quality.

mnemonic.story_en: To RESIDE means to settle down, pull your chair RE-back, and SIDE-sit there permanently.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把行李往後放（RE），在一座房子裡安穩地坐下（SIDE/sedere），意為「居住」。

example: The family chose to reside in a quiet suburb just outside the bustling city.

definition: To find a solution to a problem, dispute, or contentious matter, or to decide firmly on a course of action.

mnemonic.story_en: To RESOLVE a conflict is to completely SOLVE-untie a knotted problem so it disappears.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把死結徹底（RE）鬆開（SOLVE），讓麻煩化解，這就是「解決」問題。

example: The two countries are working together to resolve the border dispute peacefully.

definition: A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets that can be drawn on by a person or organization.

mnemonic.story_en: Natural wealth keeps SOURCE-rising up RE-again and again from the earth for human use.
mnemonic.story_zh: 能源與財富像泉水一樣不斷（RE）向上湧現（SOURCE），就成了天然的「資源」。

example: Water is a precious natural resource that must be preserved carefully.

definition: To say or do something as a reaction to something that has been said or done.

mnemonic.story_en: When a message is sent, you pledge SPOND-your answer RE-back to the sender immediately.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當別人發問，你把答案承諾並拋回（RE）去（SPOND），就是「回應」。

example: The company promised to respond to all customer complaints within 24 hours.

definition: A verbal or written answer, or a physical reaction to a specific stimulus or event.

mnemonic.story_en: Your written RESPONSE is the answer you send SPONS-back RE-to a formal invitation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 寄回（RE）去的表態與承諾（SPONS），也就是對外部刺激的「反應」或「答案」。

example: The government's slow response to the crisis was heavily criticized by the media.

definition: To bring back a previous right, practice, custom, or situation; to return something to its former condition.

mnemonic.story_en: To RESTORE a historic painting is to set it STORE-up beautifully RE-back to how it looked on day one.
mnemonic.story_zh: 重新（RE）安置與建立（STORE）古老文物的原貌，即是「修復」或「恢復」。

example: The power company worked through the night to restore electricity to the storm-damaged area.

definition: To prevent someone or something from doing something; to keep under control or limit.

mnemonic.story_en: To RE-strain bad behavior is to pull the rope STRAIN-tightly back to keep them locked.
mnemonic.story_zh: 將失控的行為用力往回（RE）拉緊（STRAIN/stringere），指的就是「抑制」。

example: He had to restrain his anger when the customer started shouting rudely.

definition: To put a limit on something, keeping it within certain boundaries, sizes, or strict parameters.

mnemonic.story_en: A STRICT-border keeps visitors locked and pulls them RE-back within a defined small space.
mnemonic.story_zh: 限制活動範圍，將邊界往回（RE）拉緊綁死（STRICT），即為「限制」。

example: The new law will restrict the sale of alcohol to minors under eighteen.

definition: To continue to have something; to keep possession of an object or hold information in memory.

mnemonic.story_en: Instead of letting an item go, you TAIN-hold it RE-back securely in your hand.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把不該流失的東西往回（RE）緊緊抓住（TAIN/tenere），代表「保留」。

example: The company managed to retain its top position in the global market despite tough competition.

definition: To move back or withdraw from a place or a difficult situation, especially during a military conflict.

mnemonic.story_en: When the army is losing, the general decides to TREAT-pull his forces RE-back into safety.
mnemonic.story_zh: 被敵軍擊敗後，把部隊往後（RE）拉（TREAT/trahere）以保全性命，即「撤退」。

example: The soldiers were ordered to retreat when the enemy forces launched a massive counter-attack.

definition: To make previously unknown or secret information known to others, or to uncover a hidden object.

mnemonic.story_en: To RE-reveal a secret is to do the opposite of VEAL-veiling it, pulling the cloth off completely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把遮蓋祕密的面紗（VEAL/velum）給反向（RE）掀開，就是「揭露」。

example: The investigation managed to reveal widespread corruption within the city government.

definition: The total amount of money received by a company or organization from its regular business activities.

mnemonic.story_en: Corporate sales ensure that cash keeps VEN-coming RE-back into the bank account every day.
mnemonic.story_zh: 賣出商品後，金錢源源不斷地回（RE）來（VEN/venire）到帳戶，即是「收入」。

example: The tech company reported a 20% increase in quarterly revenue from cloud services.

definition: To move backward, or to change a decision, direction, or order to its exact opposite.

mnemonic.story_en: To RE-reverse a car means to VERSE-turn the steering wheel and drive backward into a garage.
mnemonic.story_zh: 將方向轉（VERSE）向後面（RE），就是「逆轉」或「顛倒」。

example: The supreme court decided to reverse the lower court's original judgment.

definition: To re-examine and make alterations to a piece of writing, policy, or system to ensure accuracy.

mnemonic.story_en: You read your essay and VISE-look at it RE-again to catch errors and fix sentences.
mnemonic.story_zh: 對寫好的文章再次（RE）進行觀看（VISE/videre）與檢查，這就是「修訂」。

example: The authors had to revise the textbook chapter based on feedback from professors.

definition: A forcible overthrow of a government or social order in favor of a new system, or one complete orbit around an axis.

mnemonic.story_en: A social REVOLUTION occurs when citizens roll VOLU-over the old system to turn things around RE-completely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 將舊政權與舊秩序像輪子一樣往前滾動（VOLU）並全面翻轉（RE），即「革命」。

example: The industrial revolution marked a major turning point in human history and lifestyle.

definition: Unable to bend or be forced out of shape; not flexible, or unwilling to change strict rules.
definition_zh: 硬的；僵硬的；嚴格的；刻板的

mnemonic.story_en: A RIG-id plastic pipe is locked tight and stays RIG-stiff no matter how much force you apply.
mnemonic.story_zh: 本義是指結冰般僵硬（RIGERE），用來形容不可彎曲的物體或不可通融的「刻板」規則。

example: The military maintains a rigid hierarchy where orders must be strictly obeyed.

definition: The possibility that something unpleasant, dangerous, or harmful will happen as a result of an action.

mnemonic.story_en: Sailing a ship too close to a sharp coastal RISK-rock carries a high danger of crashing.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自航海術語，指船隻靠近暗礁（RISCO）所面臨的船毀人亡的「危險」。

example: Investing all your money in a single unstable stock carries a high financial risk.

definition: A way or course taken in getting from a starting point to a specific destination.

mnemonic.story_en: A ROUTE is a path that has been broken ROUT-open through the wild forest for travelers.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在荒野中破開（RUPTA/ROUT）障礙開闢出來的一條「路線」。

example: The GPS calculated the fastest route to avoid the heavy holiday traffic.

definition: A sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program or standard operating procedure.
definition_zh: 例行公事；常規；慣例；程序

mnemonic.story_en: You walk the exact same ROUT-path every single day until it becomes a fixed routine.
mnemonic.story_zh: 每天都走同一條開闢出來的固定路線（ROUTE），天天重複，就是「例行公事」。

example: Exercising in the morning has become an essential part of my daily routine.

definition: A small part or quantity intended to show what the whole group or mass is like.

mnemonic.story_en: A SAMPLE is pulled out of a massive batch to act as an AMPLE-example of quality.
mnemonic.story_zh: 由 example 演變而來，指拿出來做代表、供大家檢驗的「樣品」或「樣本」。

example: The quality inspector took a random sample of bottles from the production line.

definition: A threatened penalty for disobeying a law, or official permission or approval for an action.
definition_zh: 制裁；國際處罰；官方批准

mnemonic.story_en: A SANCT-ion is an official decree made holy and law by the church or high authorities.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自神聖（SANCT）的法令，在國際上指違規時面臨的「制裁」，在法律上也有「批准」之意。

example: The United Nations imposed strict economic sanctions on the nation to halt its nuclear project.

definition: A graduated range of values forming a standard system for measuring or judging something.

mnemonic.story_en: Like climbing up a steep ladder, you measure height step by step along a numerical SCALE.
mnemonic.story_zh: 本義有像梯子（SKALA）一樣一階一階的刻度，引申為測量的「刻度」或企業的「規模」。

example: The company decided to expand its business operations on a global scale.

definition: The state of being scarce or in short supply; a severe shortage of essential goods.

mnemonic.story_en: During a severe drought, food resources become SCARCE, creating widespread scarcity.
mnemonic.story_zh: 物資被拔除（SCARSUS）得所剩無幾，導致市場上極度「缺乏」與「不足」。

example: The scarcity of clean drinking water is a major issue in many developing nations.

definition: A plan for carrying out a process or procedure, giving a list of intended events and times.

mnemonic.story_en: You write your daily tasks down on a small SCHED-slip of paper to keep track of your time.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在小紙條（SCHEDULA）上寫滿重要事項與時間，就成了一份「時間表」。

example: The production manager is working hard to keep the project on schedule.

definition: A large-scale systematic plan or arrangement for attaining a particular object, or a secret plot.

mnemonic.story_en: The mastermind drew up a complex SCHE-figure on the board to coordinate the bank robbery scheme.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自希臘語的外形或圖表（SKHEMA），引申為精心策劃的「方案」或「陰謀」。

example: The city council introduced a new scheme to encourage recycling among residents.

definition: The extent of the area or subject matter that something deals with or to which it is relevant.

mnemonic.story_en: You look through a micro-SCOPE to see the entire SCOPE-range of the cell structure.
mnemonic.story_zh: 透過觀測器（SKOPOS）能看見的所有視野，就是這項研究的「範圍」。

example: The full investigation into the matter falls outside the scope of this committee.

definition: A distinct part or piece of something that has been divided or cut from a whole.

mnemonic.story_en: A large company is SEC-cut into smaller sections so each team can manage a part.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把一大塊物體切割（SECARE）成一小塊一小塊的，那一塊就是「部分」或「部門」。

example: The library has a special section dedicated exclusively to rare historical books.

definition: An area or portion that is distinct from others, especially in a country's economy or geography.

mnemonic.story_en: The economy is SEC-cut into distinct sectors, like the agricultural and tech sectors.
mnemonic.story_zh: 被切割（SECARE）出來的特定經濟或社會領域，即為「部門」或「行業」。

example: The government is trying to encourage job growth in the private sector.

definition: Protected against attack or other criminal activity; feeling safe and free from fear or anxiety.

mnemonic.story_en: When a house is protected, you live SE-without any CURA-worry or fear of thieves.
mnemonic.story_zh: 處於沒有（SE）任何憂慮（CURA）的狀態中，說明環境非常「安全的」。

example: Please make sure that all windows are secure before you leave the building.

definition: The state of being free from danger or threat, or the safety measures taken to protect a place.
definition_zh: 安全；保障；證券；防護設施

mnemonic.story_en: High airport SECURITY measures ensure that passengers travel SE-without any CUR-worry.
mnemonic.story_zh: 透過嚴密的措施達到免除（SE）憂慮（CUR）的目的，即是「安全」或「保障」。

example: The stadium upgraded its security system ahead of the international soccer match.

definition: To attempt to find, find out, or obtain something that is desired or needed.

mnemonic.story_en: In a game of hide and SEEK, you look everywhere to find your hidden friends.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自古英語，指轉動視線、花費精力去追蹤並「尋找」想要的人事物。

example: The company decided to seek financial advice before investing in the new market.

definition: To carefully choose from a group of options as being the best or most suitable.

mnemonic.story_en: You LECT-gather the finest apples and set them SE-apart from the rotten ones.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把好茶葉挑選（LECT/legere）出來並單獨分開（SE）放，這就是「精心挑選」。

example: The committee will select the best three candidates for the final interview phase.

definition: A particular order in which related events, movements, or things follow each other.

mnemonic.story_en: Numbers follow a fixed SEQ-sequence, where each item must follow the one before it.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一個接一個緊緊跟隨（SEQ/sequi）著發生的連續事件，就是「順序」。

example: The computer program executes the mathematical instructions in a logical sequence.

definition: A number of things, events, or objects of a similar kind coming one after another.

mnemonic.story_en: A book SERIES connects multiple SER-linked stories together into a complete collection.
mnemonic.story_zh: 像珍珠一樣把同類別的東西串聯（SER/serere）編排在一起，就成了「系列」。

example: The network is launching a new television series about modern architectural designs.

definition: To move or change from one position, direction, or focus to another, or a period of work time.

mnemonic.story_en: To SHIFT gears is to change and arrange your car's speed to match the road condition.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自古英語，有分割與重組安排之意，引申為焦點或位置的「移動」與「轉移」。

example: The company decided to shift its marketing focus from print media to online platforms.

definition: A state or situation in which something needed cannot be obtained in sufficient amounts.

mnemonic.story_en: When a resource falls SHORT of the demand, a severe market shortage occurs immediately.
mnemonic.story_zh: 長度或數量不夠、太短（SHORT），在市場供需上就成了「短缺」。

example: The drought caused a severe food shortage across the entire southern province.

definition: The quality of being worthy of attention; important or full of deeper meaning.

mnemonic.story_en: An event has SIGNIFICANCE when it makes FIC-a major SIGN-mark in human history books.
mnemonic.story_zh: 能夠在歷史上做出（FIC）鮮明標記（SIGN）的事情，必然具有極高的「重要性」。

example: The discovery of the new planet holds great significance for modern astronomy.

definition: Sufficiently great or important to be worthy of attention; noteworthy or expressing a hidden meaning.
definition_zh: 顯著的；重要的；有重大意義的

mnemonic.story_en: A SIGNIFICANT change makes a clear, visible SIGN-mark on the scientific chart data.
mnemonic.story_zh: 做出了（FIC）巨大標記（SIGN）的數據變化，說明這種影響是「顯著的」。

example: There has been a significant increase in online sales over the past year.

definition: Having a resemblance in appearance, character, or quantity, without being identical.

mnemonic.story_en: Twins often look SIMIL-similar because they share SIMIL-like facial features and genes.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自拉丁語，本身就是相像（SIMILIS）的意思，指兩物特徵高度「相似的」。

example: The two smartphone models are very similar in size and internal specifications.

definition: To imitate the appearance or character of a process, situation, or system, often using a computer program.

mnemonic.story_en: Astronauts use computer software to SIMUL-simulate zero gravity, creating a space-like environment.
mnemonic.story_zh: 利用程式做出一個極其相像（SIMIL）的虛擬環境，這就是「模擬」。

example: The flight training software is designed to simulate difficult weather conditions for student pilots.

definition: An area of ground on which a town, building, or monument is constructed, or a location on the internet.
definition_zh: 地點；場所; 遺跡；網站

mnemonic.story_en: The engineer visited the construction SITE to check the physical placement of the building.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自拉丁語的位置（SITUS），指某個特定的建築「工地」或網路上的「網站」。

example: The historic castle site attracts thousands of international tourists every year.

definition: The aggregate of people living together in a more or less ordered community sharing customs and laws.

mnemonic.story_en: A SOCI-ety is formed when many individual SOCI-companions gather to live and work under shared rules.
mnemonic.story_zh: 由無數個夥伴（SOCIUS）共同居住、互動而形成的群體，即是「社會」。

example: Technology has caused profound changes in the way modern society communicates.
